value.zh: 然去聖久遠，異同紛糾，苟少有仿佛，可以崇濟先典，扶明大業，有益於時，則惟患言之不能，焉得靜默，及未舉一隅，略示所存而已哉！
value.en: Yet the age was long distant from the sages, and differences and agreements were tangled. If there were even a slight resemblance by which one could exalt and aid the former canons, support and clarify the great enterprise, and benefit the time, then one should worry only that one could not say it. How could one remain silent, or merely point to one corner and sketch what one preserved?

value.zh: 夫至無者無以能生，故始生者自生也。
value.en: Utter nonbeing has no means by which it can generate life; therefore what first produces life produces itself.
value.literal: Utter nonbeing has no means by which it can generate life; therefore what first produces life produces itself.

value.zh: 自生而必體有，則有遺而生虧矣。
value.en: If what produces itself must embody being, then if being is left behind, production is deficient.
value.literal: If what produces itself must embody being, then if being is left behind, production is deficient.

value.zh: 生以有為已分，則虛無是有之所謂遺者也。
value.en: Since production takes being as its own allotment, emptiness and nonbeing are what being calls something left behind.
value.literal: Since production takes being as its own allotment, emptiness and nonbeing are what being calls something left behind.

value.zh: 故養既化之有，非無用之所能全也；
value.en: Therefore nourishing being after it has transformed is not something the function of nonbeing can make whole.
value.literal: Therefore nourishing being after it has transformed is not something the function of nonbeing can make whole.

value.zh: 理既有之眾，非無為之所能循也。
value.en: Ordering the multitude after it already exists is not something nonaction can follow through on.
value.literal: Ordering the multitude after it already exists is not something nonaction can follow through on.

value.zh: 心非事也，而制事必由於心，然不可以制事以非事，謂心為無也。
value.en: The mind is not an affair, yet regulating affairs must come from the mind; but one cannot, because regulating affairs is not itself an affair, call the mind nonbeing.
value.literal: The mind is not an affair, yet regulating affairs must come from the mind; but one cannot, because regulating affairs is not itself an affair, call the mind nonbeing.

value.zh: 匠非器也，而制器必須於匠，然不可以制器以非器，謂匠非有也。
value.en: The artisan is not the vessel, yet making vessels must require the artisan; but one cannot, because making vessels is not itself the vessel, say that the artisan is not being.
value.literal: The artisan is not the vessel, yet making vessels must require the artisan; but one cannot, because making vessels is not itself the vessel, say that the artisan is not being.

value.zh: 是以欲收重泉之鱗，非偃息之所能獲也；
value.en: Therefore if one wants to catch fish in the deep springs, it is not something lying still can obtain.
value.literal: Therefore if one wants to catch fish in the deep springs, it is not something lying still can obtain.

value.zh: 隕高墉之禽，非靜拱之所能捷也；
value.en: If one wants to bring down birds from high walls, it is not something standing quietly with folded hands can swiftly accomplish.
value.literal: If one wants to bring down birds from high walls, it is not something standing quietly with folded hands can swiftly accomplish.

value.zh: 審投弦餌之用，非無知之所能覽也。
value.en: Examining the use of casting lines and bait is not something without knowledge can perceive.
value.literal: Examining the use of casting lines and bait is not something without knowledge can perceive.

value.zh: 由此而觀，濟有者皆有也，虛無奚益於已有之群生哉！
value.en: Seen from this, what assists being is all being. What benefit do emptiness and nonbeing have for the multitude of living beings that already exist?
value.literal: Seen from this, what assists being is all being. What benefit do emptiness and nonbeing have for the multitude of living beings that already exist?

value.zh: 王衍之徒攻難交至，並莫能屈。
value.en: Wang Yan's clique besieged him with objections, yet none could break his argument.
value.literal: Wang Yan's clique besieged him with objections, yet none could break his argument.

value.zh: 又著《辯才論》，古今精義皆辨釋焉，未成而遇禍。
value.en: His unfinished "Treatise on Eloquence" surveyed classical debates but death cut it short.
value.literal: He also composed the "Treatise on Eloquence," clarifying every subtle point ancient and modern; he did not finish it before catastrophe struck.

value.zh: 楷性寬厚，與物無忤。
value.en: Genial and conciliatory, he picked no quarrels.
value.literal: Kai was tolerant and magnanimous; he contended with nothing.

value.zh: 不持儉素，每游榮貴，輒取其珍玩。
value.en: He freely accepted gifts from the mighty.
value.literal: He did not affect austerity; visiting grandees he accepted their finest curios.

value.zh: 雖車馬器服，宿昔之間，便以施諸窮乏。
value.en: By morning those luxuries reached the poor.
value.literal: Carriages, robes, vessels—overnight he gave them to the needy.

value.zh: 嘗營別宅，其從兄衍見而悅之，即以宅與衍。
value.en: Yan admired his new manor; Kai signed it over.
value.literal: He built a villa; his elder cousin Yan coveted it, so Kai gave him the house outright.

value.zh: 梁、趙二王，國之近屬，貴重當時，楷歲請二國租錢百萬，以散親族。
value.en: He diverted a million coins yearly from those princely estates to aid relatives.
value.literal: The Liang and Zhao princes were imperial kin of the highest rank; Kai annually took one million cash from their rents for kin.

value.zh: 人或譏之，楷曰：「損有餘以補不足，天之道也。」
value.en: "Redistribution follows Heaven," he replied.
value.literal: Critics sneered; Kai answered: "Taking from surplus to aid deficiency—that is Heaven's Way."

value.zh: 安於毀譽，其行己任率，皆此類也。
value.en: He shrugged at gossip and followed instinct.
value.literal: Untroubled by praise or blame, he lived candidly—always thus.

value.zh: 與山濤、和嶠並以盛德居位，帝嘗問曰：「朕應天順時，海內更始，天下風聲，何得何失？」
value.en: Together with Shan Tao and He Jiao, he held office with abundant virtue. The emperor once asked, "I respond to Heaven and follow the time, and within the seas there is a new beginning. In the voices of custom throughout the realm, what has been gained and what has been lost?"
value.literal: Together with Shan Tao and He Jiao, he held office with abundant virtue. The emperor once asked, "I respond to Heaven and follow the time, and within the seas there is a new beginning. In the voices of custom throughout the realm, what has been gained and what has been lost?"

value.zh: 楷對曰：「陛下受命，四海承風，所以未比德於堯舜者，但以賈充之徒尚在朝耳。
value.en: Kai replied, "Your Majesty has received the mandate, and the four seas follow your influence. The reason your virtue is not yet compared with Yao and Shun is only that the likes of Jia Chong are still at court.
value.literal: Kai replied, "Your Majesty has received the mandate, and the four seas follow your influence. The reason your virtue is not yet compared with Yao and Shun is only that the likes of Jia Chong are still at court.

value.zh: 方宜引天下賢人，與弘正道，不宜示人以私。」
value.en: Just now you should draw in worthy men from all under Heaven and with them broaden the correct Way; you should not show people private favor."
value.literal: Just now you should draw in worthy men from all under Heaven and with them broaden the correct Way; you should not show people private favor."

value.zh: 時任愷、庾純亦以充為言，帝乃出充為關中都督。
value.en: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him until the emperor reassigned Chong as Guanzhong area commander.
value.literal: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him; the emperor posted Chong to frontier command.

value.zh: 充納女于太子，乃止。
value.en: Chong betrothed his daughter to the crown prince, so the transfer was cancelled.
value.literal: Chong married his daughter to the crown prince, and [the transfer] then stopped.

value.zh: 平吳之後，帝方修太平之化，每延公卿，與論政道。
value.en: Pacifying Wu opened seminars on governance.
value.literal: After Wu fell the emperor cultivated Great Peace, hosting ministers to debate policy.

value.zh: 楷陳三五之風，次敘漢魏盛衰之跡。
value.en: He lectured on antiquity's golden ages versus Han-Wei cycles.
value.literal: Kai traced the Three August Ones and Five Lords, then Han and Wei's rise and fall.

value.zh: 帝稱善，坐者嘆服焉。
value.en: The throne approved and the assembly marveled.
value.literal: The emperor praised him; listeners sighed admiration.

value.zh: 楷有渴利疾，不樂處勢。
value.en: Diabetes-like thirst made central office unbearable.
value.literal: Kai suffered wasting thirst and loathed heavy responsibility.

value.zh: 王渾為楷請曰：「楷受先帝拔擢之恩，復蒙陛下寵遇，誠竭節之秋也。
value.en: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.
value.literal: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.

value.zh: 然楷性不競於物，昔為常侍，求出為河內太守；
value.en: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.
value.literal: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.

value.zh: 後為侍中，復求出為河南尹；
value.en: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.
value.literal: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.

value.zh: 與楊駿不平，求為衛尉；
value.en: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
value.literal: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

value.zh: 及轉東宮，班在時類之下，安於淡退，有識有以見其心也。
value.en: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.
value.literal: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.

value.zh: 楷今委頓，臣深憂之。
value.en: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.
value.literal: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.

value.zh: 光祿勳缺，以為可用。
value.en: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.
value.literal: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.

value.zh: 今張華在中書，王戎在尚書，足舉其契，無為復令楷入，名臣不多，當見將養，不違其志，要其遠濟之益。」
value.en: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."
value.literal: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."

value.zh: 不聽，就加光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
value.en: The throne instead piled on Household Grandee and three-duke parity.
value.literal: [The emperor] did not listen; [Kai] was additionally given Household Grandee and allowed to maintain a separate headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 及疾篤，詔遣黃門郎王衍省疾，楷回眸矚之曰：「竟未相識。」
value.en: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."
value.literal: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."

value.zh: 衍深歎其神俊。
value.en: Yan stood awed by that dying brilliance.
value.literal: Yan deeply sighed at his spiritual brilliance.

value.zh: 初，裴、王二族盛于魏晉之世，時人以為八裴方八王：徽比王祥，楷比王衍，康比王綏，綽比王澄，瓚比王敦，遐比王導，頠比王戎，邈比王玄雲。
value.en: The Pei and Wang houses flourished in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.
value.literal: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
value.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

value.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
value.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
value.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
value.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
value.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

value.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
value.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
value.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.zh: 太子不能從。
value.en: Yu ignored him.
value.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

value.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
value.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
value.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
value.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
value.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

value.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
value.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
value.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
value.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

value.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
value.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

value.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
value.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
value.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

value.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
value.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

value.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
value.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
value.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

value.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
value.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
value.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

value.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
value.en: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
value.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

value.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
value.en: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
value.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

value.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。
value.en: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
value.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.

value.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。
value.en: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
value.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.

value.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。
value.en: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
value.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

value.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。
value.en: Last twelfth month Daowen became gravely ill; the affection between father and son made us deeply pity one another.
value.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.

value.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。
value.en: His plea for son's title failed.
value.literal: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.

value.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。
value.en: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
value.literal: When illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.

value.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。
value.en: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."
value.literal: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."

value.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。
value.en: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."
value.literal: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."

value.zh: '即便作表求入。
value.en: He requested audience.
value.literal: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.

value.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。
value.en: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
value.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.

value.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。
value.en: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
value.literal: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'

value.zh: '使住空屋中坐。
value.en: They parked him in an empty room.
value.literal: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.

value.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
value.en: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
value.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

value.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。
value.en: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
value.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

value.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。
value.en: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
value.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.

value.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。
value.en: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
value.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.

value.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？
value.en: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
value.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

value.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。
value.en: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.
value.literal: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.

value.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。
value.en: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
value.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.

value.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。
value.en: Empty stomach worried him.
value.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.

value.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。
value.en: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.
value.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.

value.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！
value.en: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
value.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!

value.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？
value.en: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?
value.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?

value.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。
value.en: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.
value.literal: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

value.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。
value.en: Cornered he drank more.
value.literal: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.

value.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。
value.en: After drinking it, I became dazed and lost awareness.
value.literal: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.

value.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。
value.en: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case and said, "The emperor orders you to copy this document."
value.literal: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case, saying, 'The edict orders you to write out this document.'

value.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。
value.en: He found white and green paper inside.
value.literal: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.

value.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。
value.en: Runners said the emperor waited.
value.literal: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'

value.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。
value.en: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
value.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.

value.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。
value.en: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
value.literal: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.

value.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」
value.en: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'
value.literal: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'

value.zh: 應詹字思遠，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之孫也。
value.en: Ying Zhan, whose courtesy name was Siyuan, came from Nandun in Runan; he was the grandson of Ying Qu, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant.
value.literal: Ying Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan, was a native of Nandun in Runan, and a grandson of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.

value.zh: 詹幼孤，爲祖母所養。
value.en: He lost his parents while still a boy and was brought up by his grandmother.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was raised by his grandmother.

value.zh: 年十餘歲，祖母又終，居喪毀頓，杖而後起，遂以孝聞。
value.en: After his grandmother died when he was just past ten, he mourned until his body gave way and he needed a walking stick to stand; word of his filial piety spread.
value.literal: When he was a little over ten sui, his grandmother also died; in mourning he wasted away so badly that he could rise only with a staff, and he came to be known for his filial devotion.

value.zh: 家富於財，年又稚弱，乃請族人共居，委以資產，情若至親，世以此異焉。
value.en: The family was wealthy, but he was still a child; he asked his kinsmen to share one roof with him and handed his assets into their care, treating them as his nearest kin—an act that struck people of the time as extraordinary.
value.literal: His household was rich in wealth, and he was still very young, so he invited his clansmen to live together with him, entrusting them with his property; their feelings were like those of the closest kin, and the world marveled at this on that account.

value.zh: 弱冠知名，性質素弘雅，物雖犯而弗之校，以學藝文章稱。
value.en: After his capping he won a reputation; he was steady, broad-minded, and elegant by temperament, slow to take offense when others crossed him, and admired for his scholarship, arts, and writing.
value.literal: At the capping age he was already well known; by nature he was plain, magnanimous, and refined, and though things might offend him he did not contend with them; he was esteemed for learning, craft, and literary skill.

value.zh: 司徒何劭見之曰：「君子哉若人！」
value.en: When Situ He Shao met him, he exclaimed, “Here is a true gentleman.”
value.literal: Situ He Shao, seeing him, said, “What a gentleman this man is!”

value.zh: 敦弱冠仕州郡，辟司空府，稍遷太子舍人、尚書郎，朝士多稱之。
value.en: After his capping he served locally, entered the works directorate, rose to heir’s attendant and palace gentleman, and won wide praise at court.
value.literal: At the capping age Dun served in province and commandery, was summoned to the directorate of works, and by stages rose to Gentleman Attendant of the heir apparent and gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; court gentlemen much praised him.

value.zh: 東海王越聞，召以爲主簿。
value.en: Sima Yue of the East Sea made him chief clerk.
value.literal: Prince Sima Yue of the East Sea heard of him and summoned him as chief clerk.

value.zh: 王彌逼洛，敦及胡毋輔之勸越擊王彌，而王衍、潘滔共執不聽，敦庭爭苦至，眾咸壯之。
value.en: As Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Dun and Hu Wuzhi begged Sima Yue to attack; Wang Yan and Pan Tao blocked the plan while Dun shouted himself hoarse in open court—the crowd admired his nerve.
value.literal: When Wang Mi pressed Luoyang, Dun together with Hu Wuzhi urged Yue to strike Wang Mi, but Wang Yan and Pan Tao together seized control and would not listen; Dun argued bitterly in court to the utmost, and the crowd all thought him heroic.

value.zh: 出補汝南內史。
value.en: He went out as interior minister of Runan.
value.literal: He went out to fill the vacancy as interior minister of Runan.

value.zh: 元帝之爲鎮東，請爲軍諮祭酒，不就。
value.en: Emperor Yuan as east-general wanted him as army libationer; he declined.
value.literal: When Emperor Yuan was east-general, he asked Dun to be libationer-adviser of the army, but Dun did not accept.

value.zh: 征南將軍山簡以爲司馬。
value.en: Shan Jian named him marshal.
value.literal: General Who Conquers the South, Shan Jian, made him marshal.

value.zh: 尋而王如、杜曾相繼爲亂，簡乃使敦監沔北七郡軍事、振威將軍、領江夏相，戍夏口。
value.en: When Wang Ru and Du Zeng revolted, Shan Jian put him over seven northern Han commanderies as General Who Rouses Might and Jiangxia administrator, based at Xiakou.
value.literal: Soon Wang Ru and Du Zeng rose in succession; Jian then had Dun supervise military affairs in seven commanderies north of the Mian, as General Who Rouses Might, concurrently grand administrator of Jiangxia, garrisoned at Xiakou.

value.zh: 敦攻討沔中皆平。
value.en: He cleared the Han basin by force.
value.literal: Dun attacked and campaigned until all the middle Han was pacified.

value.zh: 既而杜弢寇湘中，加敦征討大都督。
value.en: When Du Tao struck Xiang, he became grand commander of suppression.
value.literal: Afterward Du Tao raided Xiang commanderies, and Dun was additionally named supreme area commander for conquest.

value.zh: 伐弢有功，賜爵安陵亭侯。
value.en: Crushing Du Tao won him the village marquisate of Anling.
value.literal: For merit in campaigning against Tao he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Anling.

value.zh: 鎮東大將軍王敦請爲軍司。
value.en: Wang Dun, east-guarding general, recruited him as army director.
value.literal: General Who Guards the East, Wang Dun, asked him to be army director.

value.zh: 朱瑄，宋州下邑人也。
value.en: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.
value.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.

value.zh: 父慶，里之豪右，以攻剽販鹽為事，吏捕之伏法。
value.en: His father Qing, a village strongman, lived by banditry and salt-running until the authorities caught and executed him.
value.literal: His father Qing was a local magnate who made his living by raiding and smuggling salt; officials seized him and he was executed by law.

value.zh: 瑄坐父罪以笞免。
value.en: Xuan was caned and dismissed because of his father's offense.
value.literal: Xuan, implicated in his father's crime, was flogged and released.

value.zh: 因入王敬武軍為小校。
value.en: He then joined Wang Jingwu's forces as a low-ranking officer.
value.literal: Thereupon he entered Wang Jingwu's army as a junior officer.

value.zh: 唐中和二年，諫議大夫張浚征兵於青州，敬武遣將曹全晸率軍赴之，以瑄隸焉。
value.en: In Tang Zhonghe year 2, Censor Zhang Jun mustered troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu dispatched Cao Quanzhen's army to answer the call, and Xuan went with it.
value.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe of Tang, Remonstrance Censor Zhang Jun raised troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu sent the general Cao Quanzhen with an army to join him, with Xuan attached to that force.

value.zh: 以戰功累遷列校。
value.en: Repeated victories raised him through the ranks of field officers.
value.literal: Through battle merit he was repeatedly promoted among the column commanders.

value.zh: 賊敗出關，全晸以本軍還鎮。
value.en: After the rebels broke and fled beyond the passes, Quanzhen marched his own troops back to their post.
value.literal: When the rebels were defeated and driven out of the passes, Quanzhen returned to garrison with his original army.

value.zh: 會鄆帥薛崇卒，部將崔君預據城叛，全晸攻之，殺君預自為留後。
value.en: Yan commander Xue Chong died; his subordinate Cui Junyu rebelled and held the city. Quanzhen stormed it, killed Junyu, and declared himself acting commissioner.
value.literal: When Yan military commissioner Xue Chong died, his officer Cui Junyu seized the city in revolt; Quanzhen attacked, killed Junyu, and made himself acting commissioner.

value.zh: 瑄以功授濮州刺史、鄆州馬步軍都將。
value.en: For his service Xuan received Pu prefecture and command of Yanzhou's combined cavalry and infantry.
value.literal: Xuan, for merit, was appointed prefect of Pu and commander of Yan's horse-and-foot forces.

value.zh: 光啟初，魏博韓允中攻鄆，全晸為其所害。
value.en: Early in the Guangqi reign Han Yunzhong of Weibo attacked Yan, and Quanzhen fell in the fighting.
value.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Weibo's Han Yunzhong attacked Yan; Quanzhen was killed by him.

value.zh: 瑄據城自固。
value.en: Xuan barricaded himself inside the city.
value.literal: Xuan held the city and fortified himself.

value.zh: 三軍推為留後。
value.en: The army proclaimed him acting commissioner.
value.literal: The three armies pushed him to be acting commissioner.

value.zh: 允中敗，朝廷以瑄為天平軍節度使，累加官至檢校太尉、同平章事。
value.en: After Yunzhong's defeat the throne appointed Xuan commissioner of Tianping; he eventually reached honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
value.literal: When Yunzhong was defeated, the court made Xuan military commissioner of Tianping, and he rose in rank to honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

value.zh: 太祖初鎮大梁，兵威未振，連歲為秦宗權所圍，士不解甲，危殆日數四。
value.en: When the Founder first governed Daliang his power was still weak; Qin Zongquan besieged him year after year, troops never out of mail, danger threatening several times daily.
value.literal: When the Founder first held Daliang, his military prestige was not yet established; year after year he was besieged by Qin Zongquan, his men never doffing armor, peril coming several times a day.

value.zh: 太祖以瑄同宗，早兄事之，乃遣使求援於瑄。
value.en: Calling Xuan kin, the Founder had long treated him as an elder brother and now begged him for help.
value.literal: The Founder, treating Xuan as a clansman, had long addressed him as elder brother, and sent envoys to seek aid from Xuan.

value.zh: 光啟末，宗權急攻大梁，瑄與弟瑾率兗、鄆之師來援，大敗蔡賊，解圍而遁。
value.en: Late in Guangqi, Zongquan hammered Daliang; Xuan and Jin marched troops from Yan and Yanzhou, crushed the Cai army, broke the siege, and retired.
value.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Zongquan pressed the attack on Daliang; Xuan and his younger brother Jin led Yan and Yanzhou forces to the rescue, routed the Cai rebels, lifted the siege, and withdrew.

value.zh: 太祖感其力，厚禮以歸之。
value.en: Grateful for the rescue, the Founder honored them lavishly on their departure.
value.literal: The Founder, grateful for their effort, sent them home with rich courtesy.

value.zh: 先是，瑄、瑾駐於大梁，睹太祖軍士驍勇，私心愛之。
value.en: While stationed at Daliang, Xuan and Jin had seen how fierce the Founder's troops were and coveted them.
value.literal: Earlier, while Xuan and Jin were encamped at Daliang, they saw the Founder's soldiers were fierce, and secretly admired them.

value.zh: 及歸，厚懸金帛於界上以誘焉。
value.en: Back home they posted rich bounties of gold and silk along the frontier to lure deserters.
value.literal: On returning home they hung out heavy rewards of gold and silk on the border to entice them.

value.zh: 諸軍貪其厚利，私遁者甚眾。
value.en: Many of the Founder's men slipped away for the generous pay.
value.literal: The various armies, greedy for the rich profit, deserted in great numbers.

value.zh: 太祖移牒以讓之，瑄來詞不遜，由是始構隙焉。
value.en: The Founder rebuked him in writing; Xuan answered rudely, and enmity began.
value.literal: The Founder sent a written protest; Xuan came with insolent words, and from this the rift began.

value.zh: 及秦宗權敗，太祖移軍攻時溥於徐州。
value.en: After Zongquan's fall the Founder turned his armies on Shi Pu at Xuzhou.
value.literal: When Qin Zongquan was defeated, the Founder shifted his army to attack Shi Pu at Xuzhou.

value.zh: 時瑄方右溥，乃遣使來告太祖曰：「巢、權繼為蛇虺，毒螫中原，與君把臂同盟，輔車相依。
value.en: Xuan was then siding with Pu and wrote the Founder: "Chao and Zongquan were serpents in turn, stinging the heartland; we clasped arms as allies, dependent as chariot wheels.
value.literal: At that time Xuan was backing Pu, and sent an envoy to tell the Founder: "Huang Chao and Zongquan in succession were vipers, poisoning the Central Plain; you and I clasped arms in alliance, cheek by jowl as in a chariot.

value.zh: 今賊已平殄，人粗聊生，吾弟宜念遠圖，不可自相魚肉。
value.en: The rebels are gone and men barely survive; brother, keep the larger design—do not devour each other.
value.literal: Now the bandits are wiped out and people barely live again; my younger brother should think of the long view and not tear one another apart like fish and flesh.

value.zh: 或行人之失辭，疆吏之逾法，可以理遣，未得便睽和好。
value.en: A courier's slip or a frontier officer's breach can be reasoned away; do not break our bond lightly.
value.literal: Perhaps a traveler's loose word or a border officer's excess may be settled by reason; you must not lightly break the good understanding.

value.zh: 投鼠忌器，弟幸思之。」
value.en: Strike the rat but spare the vessel—brother, weigh that."
value.literal: When casting at a rat, one fears the vessel—brother, think on this."

value.zh: 太祖方怒時溥通於孫儒，不從其言。
value.en: The Founder, furious that Pu was colluding with Sun Ru, ignored the plea.
value.literal: The Founder was then angry that Pu was in league with Sun Ru and did not heed his words.

value.zh: 及龐師古攻徐州，瑄出師來援，太祖深銜之。
value.en: When Pang Shigu besieged Xuzhou, Xuan came to Pu's aid, and the Founder never forgave it.
value.literal: When Pang Shigu attacked Xuzhou, Xuan marched out to aid Pu; the Founder deeply resented it.

value.zh: 徐既平，太祖並兵以攻鄆，自景福元年冬遣朱友裕領軍渡濟，至乾寧三年宿軍齊、鄆間，大小凡數十戰，語在《太祖紀》中。
value.en: Once Xuzhou fell he massed troops against Yan: from winter of Jingfu 1 Zhu Youyu crossed the Ji, and by Qianning 3 armies lay between Qi and Yan in dozens of clashes recorded in the 《Founder's Annals》.
value.literal: After Xu was pacified, the Founder united his forces to attack Yan; from winter of Jingfu year 1 he sent Zhu Youyu with an army across the Ji, until in Qianning year 3 he camped between Qi and Yan, fighting great and small battles several tens of times, as told in the 《Founder's Annals》.

value.zh: 自是野無人耕，屬城悉為我有。
value.en: Fields lay empty; every subordinate city fell to him.
value.literal: From then the countryside was untilled; all dependent prefectures became his.

value.zh: 瑄乃遣人求救於太原，李克用遣其將李承嗣、史儼等援之。
value.en: Xuan appealed to Taiyuan; Li Keyong sent Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and other generals to help.
value.literal: Xuan then sent men to beg rescue from Taiyuan; Li Keyong dispatched his generals Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and others to aid him.

value.zh: 尋為羅宏信所扼，援路既絕，瑄、瑾竟敗。
value.en: Luo Hongxin soon blocked the road; aid failed, and Xuan and Jin were ruined.
value.literal: Soon they were choked off by Luo Hongxin; the relief route cut, Xuan and Jin were defeated at last.

value.zh: 乾寧四年正月，龐師古攻陷鄆州，遁至中都北，匿於民家，為其所箠，並妻榮氏擒之來獻，俱斬於汴橋下。
value.en: In Qianning 4, month 1, Pang Shigu captured Yan. Xuan fled north of Zhongdu and hid in a peasant home; the family thrashed and seized him and Lady Rong, and both were executed at Bian Bridge.
value.literal: In the first month of Qianning year 4, Pang Shigu took Yanzhou; fleeing north of Zhongdu, hiding in a commoner's house, he was beaten by the household, and together with his wife Lady Rong was seized and presented; both were beheaded below Bian Bridge.

value.zh: 既而為茂貞左右石簡顒等間之，免其軍政，寓於岐下，掩關曆年。
value.en: Courtiers slandered him; he lived under Qi in seclusion for years.
value.literal: Soon he was set aside from military government by Maozhen's close associates Shi Jian'e and others; he dwelt under Qi, shutting his gate for years.

value.zh: 茂貞猶子繼崇鎮秦州，因來寧覲，言知俊途窮至此，不宜以讒嫉見疑，茂貞乃誅簡顒等以安其心。
value.en: Nephew Jichong pleaded for Zhijun; Maozhen executed the slanderers to reassure him.
value.literal: Maozhen's nephew Jichong governed Qin prefecture; coming to pay respects he said Zhijun, driven to extremity, should not be suspected through slander; Maozhen then executed Jian'e and others to calm his heart.

value.zh: 繼崇又請令知俊挈家居秦州，以就豐給，茂貞從之。
value.en: Jichong invited Zhijun's family to Qin; Maozhen agreed.
value.literal: Jichong again asked that Zhijun be allowed to bring his household to live at Qin to enjoy abundance; Maozhen consented.

value.zh: 未幾，邠州亂，茂貞命知俊討之。
value.en: Bin rebelled; Maozhen sent Zhijun to suppress it.
value.literal: Before long, Bin prefecture rebelled; Maozhen ordered Zhijun to suppress it.

value.zh: 時邠州都校李保衡納款於朝廷，末帝遣霍彥威率眾先入於邠，知俊遂圍其城，半載不能下。
value.en: Li Baoheng had surrendered to Liang; Huo Yanwei entered Bin first; Zhijun besieged it six months in vain.
value.literal: At that time Bin's commander Li Baoheng had submitted to the court; the Last Emperor sent Huo Yanwei with troops to enter Bin first; Zhijun then besieged the city; half a year could not take it.

value.zh: 會李繼崇以秦州降於蜀，知俊妻孥皆遷於成都，遂解邠州之圍而歸岐陽。
value.en: Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu; Zhijun's family was taken to Chengdu; he abandoned Bin and returned to Qiyang.
value.literal: When Li Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu, Zhijun's wife and children were all moved to Chengdu; he then lifted the siege of Bin and returned to Qiyang.

value.zh: 以舉家入蜀，終慮猜忌，因與親信百餘人夜斬關奔蜀。
value.en: Fearing suspicion after his family went to Shu, he fled by night with a hundred men.
value.literal: Because his whole household had entered Shu, he finally feared suspicion; with more than a hundred trusted men he cut the pass by night and fled to Shu.

value.zh: 王建待之甚至，即授偽武信軍節度使，尋命將兵伐岐，不克，班師，因圍隴州，獲其帥桑宏誌以歸。
value.en: Wang Jian honored him as Wuxin commissioner; he failed against Qi, took Long and Sang Hongzhi, and returned.
value.literal: Wang Jian treated him to the utmost; he was at once made false Wuxin military commissioner; soon he was ordered to lead troops against Qi without success and withdrew; then he besieged Long prefecture, took its commander Sang Hongzhi, and returned.

value.zh: 久之，復命為都統，再領軍伐岐。
value.en: Later he was made overall commander and marched on Qi again.
value.literal: After a long time he was again ordered as overall commander and again led troops against Qi.

value.zh: 時部將皆王建舊人，多違節度，不成功而還，蜀人因而毀之。
value.en: At the time his subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they returned without success, and the Shu people slandered him for it.
value.literal: At that time the subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they did not succeed and returned; Shu men therefore slandered him.

value.zh: 先是，王建雖加寵待，然亦忌之，嘗謂近侍曰：「吾漸衰耗，恒思身後。
value.en: Jian favored yet feared him and told aides, "I age and think of what follows my death.
value.literal: Earlier, though Wang Jian added favor and treatment, he also was jealous; he once told close attendants: "I gradually decline and constantly think of after my death.

value.zh: 劉知俊非爾輩能駕馭，不如早為之所。」
value.en: Zhijun is not for you to control—deal with him early."
value.literal: Liu Zhijun is not what you can drive and rein—better early do something about him."

value.zh: 又嫉其名者於裏巷間作謠言云：「黑牛出圈棕繩斷。」
value.en: Enemies spread a rhyme: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope snaps."
value.literal: Those who envied his name also made a street song in the lanes: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope breaks."

value.zh: 知俊色黔而醜生，棕繩者，王氏子孫皆以「宗」、「承」為名，故以此構之。
value.en: Zhijun was dark and ugly; "palm rope" punned on Wang names using Zong and Cheng.
value.literal: Zhijun's complexion was dark and he was born ugly; "palm rope" means Wang's sons and grandsons all used "Zong" and "Cheng" in their names—thus they framed him with this.

value.zh: 偽蜀天漢元年冬十二月，建遣人捕知俊，斬於成都府之炭市。
value.en: False-Shu Tianhan 1, month 12, Jian had him beheaded at Chengdu's charcoal market.
value.literal: In the twelfth month of winter of false-Shu Tianhan year 1, Jian sent men to seize Zhijun and behead him at the charcoal market of Chengdu prefecture.

value.zh: 及王衍嗣偽位，以其子嗣禋尚偽峨眉長公主，拜駙馬都尉。
value.en: Under Wang Yan his son Sichen married the Emei princess and became chief son-in-law.
value.literal: When Wang Yan succeeded the false throne, his son Sichen married the false Emei senior princess and was appointed Chief Son-in-law.

value.zh: 後唐同光末，隨例遷於洛，卒。
value.en: At Later Tang Tongguang he moved to Luoyang and died.
value.literal: At the end of Later Tang Tongguang, following precedent he moved to Luo and died.

value.zh: 同光二年夏五月己亥，帝御文明殿，冊齊王張全義為太尉。
value.en: On jihai in summer of Tongguang 2 Cunxu invested Zhang Quanyi as Prince of Qi and Grand Commandant at Wenming Hall.
value.literal: Summer, fifth month, jihai, Tongguang year 2: the Emperor took Wenming Hall to invest Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi as Grand Commandant.

value.zh: 禮畢，全義赴尚書省領事，左諫議大夫竇專不降階，為御史所劾，專援引舊典，宰相不能詰，寢而不行。
value.en: After the rite Quanyi took office at the Directorate; Dou Zhuan refused to step down and was impeached; citing precedent, he left the ministers unable to answer and the case died.
value.literal: When the rite was done Quanyi went to the Directorate to take up office; Left Remonstrance Councillor Dou Zhuan did not descend the steps, was impeached by the censorate, cited old precedent, and the chief ministers could not rebut it—the matter was shelved.

value.zh: 庚子，太常卿李燕卒。
value.en: On gengzi Li Yan, Director of Ceremonies, died.
value.literal: On gengzi Director of Ceremonies Li Yan died.

value.zh: 壬寅，以教坊使陳俊為景州刺史，內園使儲德源為憲州刺史，皆梁之伶人也。
value.en: On renyin Chen Jun of the Music Bureau became Jing prefect and Chu Deyuan of the Inner Gardens Xian prefect—both Liang actors.
value.literal: On renyin Chen Jun, commissioner of the Music Bureau, was made Jing prefect, and Chu Deyuan, commissioner of the Inner Gardens, Xian prefect—both were Liang actor-retainers.

value.zh: 初，帝平梁，俊與德源皆為寵伶周匝所薦，帝因許除郡，郭崇韜以為不可，伶官言之者眾，帝密召崇韜謂之曰：「予已許除郡，經年未行，我慚見二人，卿當屈意行之。」
value.en: When Cunxu conquered Liang, Zhou Zha had recommended Jun and Deyuan for posts; Cunxu had promised them commands but Guo Chongtao objected; many actors pressed the case; Cunxu secretly told Guo, "I promised them prefectures a year ago and am ashamed to face them—humor me."
value.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor had pacified Liang, Jun and Deyuan had both been recommended by his favored actor Zhou Zha; he had promised them prefectures; Guo Chongtao held it impossible, yet many actor-officials spoke for it; the Emperor secretly summoned Chongtao and said, "I already promised them prefectures and for a year have not acted—I am ashamed to face the two of them; you must bend your will and carry it out."

value.zh: 故有是命。
value.en: Hence these appointments.
value.literal: Hence this order.

value.zh: 秋七月戊戌朔，故宣武軍節度使李存審男彥超進其父牙兵八千七百人。
value.en: On the wuxu new moon of the seventh month Yanchao presented his late father Li Cunshen's guard of 8,700 men.
value.literal: Seventh month, wuxu new moon: the late Xuanyang military commissioner Li Cunshen's son Yanchao presented his father's personal guard of eight thousand seven hundred men.

value.zh: 己亥，中書門下奏：「每年南郊壇四祠祭，太微宮五薦獻，並宰臣攝太尉行事，惟太廟遣庶僚行事，此後太廟祠祭，亦望差宰臣行事。」
value.en: "On jihai the Secretariat asked that temple rites, like altar and Taiwei offerings, be performed by chief ministers rather than junior staff."
value.literal: On jihai the Secretariat memorialized: "Each year at the southern altar the four shrine offerings and at Taiwei Palace the five presentations are all performed by chief ministers acting as libationer; only the Imperial Temple sends junior officials—hereafter Imperial Temple offerings should also be assigned to chief ministers."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: Approved.
value.literal: It was approved.

value.zh: 乙巳，汴州雍丘縣大風，拔木傷稼。
value.en: On yisi Yongqiu in Bianzhou had a wind that uprooted trees and ruined crops.
value.literal: On yisi Yongqiu county in Bianzhou had a great wind that uprooted trees and damaged crops.

value.zh: 曹州大雨，平地水三尺。
value.en: Caozhou flooded three feet deep on level ground.
value.literal: Caozhou had heavy rain and three feet of water on level ground.

value.zh: 丙午，以襄州節度使孔為潞州節度使，李存霸為鄆州節度使。
value.en: On bingwu Kong Qing, military governor of Xiang Prefecture, was made military governor of Lu Prefecture, and Li Cunba was made military governor of Yun Prefecture.
value.literal: On bingwu Xiang military commissioner Kong was made Luzhou military commissioner, and Li Cunba was made Yun military commissioner.

value.zh: 乙酉，幸龍門之雷山，祭天神，從北俗之舊事也。
value.en: On yiyou Cunxu sacrificed at Thunder Mountain on Longmen, following a northern custom.
value.literal: On yiyou the Emperor went to Thunder Mountain at Longmen to sacrifice to Heaven—following the northern custom of old.

value.zh: 辛亥，以鄆州副使李紹珙為襄州留後，以前澤州刺史董璋為邠州留後。
value.en: On xinhai Li Shaogong became Xiang regent, and Dong Zhang became Binzhou regent.
value.literal: On xinhai Yan deputy commissioner Li Shaogong was made Xiang regent; former Ze prefect Dong Zhang was made Bin regent.

value.zh: 戊午，西川王衍遣偽署戶部侍郎歐陽彬來朝貢，稱「大蜀皇帝上書大唐皇帝」。
value.en: On wuwu Wang Yan of Shu sent Ouyang Bin as tribute envoy, signing as "Great Shu Emperor to Great Tang Emperor."
value.literal: On wuwu Shu ruler Wang Yan sent his false-appointed Vice Minister of Revenue Ouyang Bin to court with tribute, styling himself "Great Shu Emperor writing to the Great Tang Emperor."

value.zh: 庚申，以應州為雲州屬郡，升新州為威塞軍節度使，以媯、儒、武等州為屬郡。
value.en: On gengshen Ying was attached to Yun and Xin became Weisai commissioner over Ji, Ru, and Wu.
value.literal: On gengshen Ying prefecture was made a subordinate of Yun prefecture; Xin was raised to Weisai military commissioner with Ji, Ru, and Wu as subordinates.

value.zh: 壬戌，皇子繼岌妻王氏封魏國夫人。
value.en: On renxu Jiji's wife Lady Wang was made Lady of Wei state.
value.literal: On renxu the wife of Prince Jiji, Lady Wang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei state.

value.zh: 幽州奏，契丹安巴堅東攻渤海。
value.en: Youzhou said Khitan leader Ambagyan was attacking Bohai in the east.
value.literal: Youzhou reported that the Khitan Ambagyan was attacking Bohai eastward.

value.zh: 開運二年夏五月丙申朔，帝御崇元殿受朝，大赦天下。
value.en: In Kaiyun 2, on the first day bingshen of the fifth summer month, the emperor held court at Chongyuan Hall, received homage, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
value.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, on the first day bingshen of the fifth summer month, the emperor took the throne at Chongyuan Hall to receive court homage and proclaimed a general amnesty for all under Heaven.

value.zh: 丁酉，以右衛上將軍馬萬為左金吾上將軍致仕。
value.en: On dingyou Ma Wan, General of the Right Guard, was retired as General of the Left Golden Chancellery.
value.literal: On dingyou, Ma Wan, General of the Right Guard, was made retired General of the Left Golden Chancellery.

value.zh: 戊戌，陜州節度使宋彥筠移鎮鄧州，澶州節度使何建移鎮河陽。
value.en: On wuxu Song Yanyun moved from Shaan to Deng Prefecture, and He Jian from Chan to Heyang.
value.literal: On wuxu, Song Yanyun, military commissioner of Shaan Prefecture, was transferred to Deng Prefecture, and He Jian, military commissioner of Chan Prefecture, was transferred to Heyang.

value.zh: 以左神武統軍潘環為澶州節度使，以宣徽北院使李彥韜遙領壽州節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使，以滄州節度使田武遙領夔州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使。
value.en: Pan Huan became commissioner of Chan; Li Yantao held Shou remotely while commanding the palace cavalry; Tian Wu held Kui remotely while commanding the palace infantry.
value.literal: Pan Huan, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made military commissioner of Chan Prefecture; Li Yantao, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was given concurrent remote command of Shou Prefecture and made commander of the Palace Guards Cavalry; Tian Wu, military commissioner of Cang Prefecture, was given concurrent remote command of Kui Prefecture and made commander of the Palace Guards Infantry.

value.zh: 辛亥，白虹貫日。
value.en: On xinhai a white rainbow spanned the sun.
value.literal: On xinhai, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

value.zh: 壬子，宰臣桑維翰、劉句、李崧、和凝並加階爵。
value.en: On renzi chief ministers Sang Weihan, Liu Xu, Li Song, and He Ning all received higher ranks and fiefs.
value.literal: On renzi, the chief ministers Sang Weihan, Liu Xu, Li Song, and He Ning were all advanced in rank and enfeoffment.

value.zh: 禮部尚書竇貞固改刑部尚書，太常寺卿王松改工部尚書。
value.en: Dou Zhengu moved from Rites to Justice, and Wang Song from Ceremonies to Works.
value.literal: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Rites, was changed to Minister of Justice; Wang Song, Director of the Directorate of Ceremonies, was changed to Minister of Works.

value.zh: 以尚書左丞龍敏為太常卿；
value.en: Long Min, Left Vice Director of State Affairs, became Director of Ceremonies;
value.literal: Long Min, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Director of Ceremonies;

value.zh: 以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎李慎儀為尚書左丞；
value.en: Li Shenyi, Hanlin chief academician and Vice Minister of War, became Left Vice Director of State Affairs;
value.literal: Li Shenyi, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs;

value.zh: 以御史中丞張允為兵部侍郎、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨；
value.en: Zhang Yun, Censor-in-Chief, became Vice Minister of War and drafter of rescripts and Hanlin chief academician;
value.literal: Zhang Yun, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of War, drafter of imperial rescripts, and appointed Hanlin Academician-in-Chief;

value.zh: 以左諫議大夫顏衎為御史中丞；
value.en: Yan Kan, Left Remonstrance Counselor, became Censor-in-Chief;
value.literal: Yan Kan, Left Remonstrance Counselor, was made Censor-in-Chief;

value.zh: 〈（《宋史·顏衎傳》：喪亂之後，朝綱不振，衎執憲頗有風采，嘗上言：「才除御史者旋授外藩賓佐，復有以私故細事求假外拜，州郡無參謁之儀，出入失風憲之體，漸恐四方得以輕易，百辟無所準繩。
value.en: (Song History, biography of Yan Kan: After the civil wars court discipline had slackened; Kan enforced the law with notable vigor and once memorialized: "Newly appointed censors are immediately sent as staff to frontier prefectures, and others use petty private pretexts to leave the capital for provincial posts. Prefectures then lack proper audience protocol, and the censorate loses its dignity—soon the realm may hold it in contempt and officials will have no standard.
value.literal: (Biography of Yan Kan in the Song History: After the disorders, court discipline was slack; Kan in enforcing the law showed considerable authority and once memorialized: "Those just made censors are immediately appointed as staff to outer prefectures; moreover some seek leave for minor private matters to go out and take provincial posts, so that prefectures have no protocol for audiences, and coming and going lose the dignity proper to the censorate—gradually the four quarters may take things lightly and the hundred officials have no standard to follow.

value.zh: 請自今藩鎮幕僚，勿得任臺官；
value.en: Henceforth let prefectural staff not hold censorate posts;
value.literal: I request that from now on prefectural staff may not hold censorate posts;

value.zh: 雖親王宰相出鎮，亦不得奏充賓佐；
value.en: even when princes or chief ministers take field commands, they may not be named as staff;
value.literal: even when imperial princes or chief ministers go out to command prefectures, they may not be recommended as staff;

value.zh: 非奉制勘事，勿得出京；
value.en: and except on imperial commission to investigate, censors may not leave the capital;
value.literal: except on imperial commission to investigate matters, they may not leave the capital;

value.zh: 自余不令釐雜務。」
value.en: nor handle miscellaneous duties."
value.literal: as for the rest, do not allow them to take on miscellaneous duties."

value.zh: 詔惟辟召入幕，余從其請。）〉
value.en: The edict allowed only imperial summons to enter staffs; the rest was approved.)〉
value.literal: An edict allowed only those summoned by imperial appointment to enter staffs; the rest of his requests were approved.)〉

value.zh: 以兵部侍郎、宏文館學士、判館事田敏為國子祭酒；
value.en: Tian Min, Vice Minister of War and Hongwen academician, became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education;
value.literal: Tian Min, Vice Minister of War, academician of the Hongwen Hall, and overseer of the hall, was made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education;

value.zh: 以戶部侍郎段希堯為兵部侍郎；
value.en: Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue, became Vice Minister of War;
value.literal: Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Minister of War;

value.zh: 以工部侍郎邊蔚為戶部侍郎，依前權知開封府事；
value.en: Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Works, became Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining acting charge of Kaifeng;
value.literal: Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Works, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and continued as before as acting overseer of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs;

value.zh: 以左散騎常侍李式為工部侍郎；
value.en: Li Shi, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, became Vice Minister of Works;
value.literal: Li Shi, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Vice Minister of Works;

value.zh: 以給事中王仁裕為左散騎常侍。
value.en: Wang Renyu, Supervising Secretary, became Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
value.literal: Wang Renyu, Supervising Secretary, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

value.zh: 甲寅，以華州節度使趙瑩為開封尹，以皇弟開封尹重睿為秦州節度使，以宣徽南院使劉繼勛為華州節度使，以前鄆州節度使張從恩為晉州節度使。
value.en: On jiayin Zhao Ying became Prefect of Kaifeng; the emperor's brother Chongrui left Kaifeng for Qin; Liu Jixun took Hua; and former Yun commissioner Zhang Cong'en took Jin.
value.literal: On jiayin, Zhao Ying, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, was made Prefect of Kaifeng; the emperor's younger brother Chongrui, Prefect of Kaifeng, was made military commissioner of Qin Prefecture; Liu Jixun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made military commissioner of Hua Prefecture; Zhang Cong'en, former military commissioner of Yun Prefecture, was made military commissioner of Jin Prefecture.

value.zh: 丙辰，杜威來朝。
value.en: On bingchen Du Wei presented himself at court.
value.literal: On bingchen, Du Wei came to court.

value.zh: 定州奏，大風雹，北嶽廟殿宇樹木悉摧拔之。
value.en: Ding Prefecture reported that wind and hail had destroyed the halls and trees of the Northern Marchmount Temple.
value.literal: Ding Prefecture reported that a great wind and hail had utterly uprooted the halls and trees of the Northern Marchmount Temple.

value.zh: 秋九月壬辰，鄆州節度使、侍衛親軍都指揮使李守貞加兼侍中，滑州節度使皇甫遇進封邠國公，相州節度使張彥澤加檢校太尉。
value.en: On renchen of the ninth autumn month Li Shouzhen of Yun became concurrent Palace Attendant, Huangfu Yu of Hua was made Duke of Bin, and Zhang Yanze of Xiang acting Grand Marshal.
value.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on renchen, Li Shouzhen, military commissioner of Yun Prefecture and commander of the Palace Guards Personal Army, was made concurrent Palace Attendant; Huangfu Yu, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, was advanced to Duke of Bin; Zhang Yanze, military commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, was given acting Grand Marshal.

value.zh: 甲午，以權知威武軍節度使李宏達為檢校太尉、同平章事，充福建節度使，知閩國事。
value.en: On jiawu Li Hongda of Weiwu became acting Grand Marshal, Chief Counselor, Fujian commissioner, and overseer of Min.
value.literal: On jiawu, Li Hongda, acting military commissioner of the Weiwu Army, was made acting Grand Marshal, Chief Counselor, military commissioner of Fujian, and overseer of Min affairs.

value.zh: 乙未，前商州刺史李俊賜自盡，坐與親妹奸及行劍斫殺女使，又殺部曲孫漢榮，強奸其妻，準法棄市，詔賜死於家。
value.en: On yiwei former Shang prefect Li Jun was allowed to kill himself at home for incest with his sister, murdering a maid and retainer Sun Hanrong and raping Sun's wife—a capital crime commuted to death at home.
value.literal: On yiwei, Li Jun, former prefect of Shang Prefecture, was granted permission to take his own life for having committed incest with his younger sister by blood, drawn his sword and hacked a maid to death, also killed his retainer Sun Hanrong, and raped Sun's wife; by law he deserved execution in the marketplace, but an edict allowed him to die at home.

value.zh: 己亥，張彥澤奏，破蕃賊於定州界，斬首二十餘級，追襲百餘里，生擒蕃將四人，摘得金耳環二副進呈。
value.en: On jihai Zhang Yanze reported defeating barbarians on the Ding border, taking twenty heads, pursuing a hundred li, capturing four generals, and presenting gold earrings as trophies.
value.literal: On jihai, Zhang Yanze reported breaking barbarian forces at the Ding Prefecture border, taking more than twenty heads, pursuing over a hundred li, capturing four barbarian generals alive, and presenting two pairs of gold earrings taken as trophies.

value.zh: 癸卯，太原奏，破契丹於楊武谷，殺七千餘人。
value.en: On guimao Taiyuan reported defeating the Khitan at Yangwu Valley with seven thousand killed.
value.literal: On guimao, Taiyuan reported defeating the Khitan at Yangwu Valley and killing more than seven thousand.

value.zh: 甲辰，以天策上將軍、江南諸道都統、楚王馬希範兼諸道兵馬都元帥。
value.en: On jiachen Chu prince Ma Xifan became concurrent commander-in-chief of all circuits' forces.
value.literal: On jiachen, Ma Xifan, Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem, overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits, and Prince of Chu, was made concurrent commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and horses.

value.zh: 詔開封府，以霖雨不止，應京城公私僦舍錢放一月。
value.en: Kaifeng was ordered to remit one month's rent on capital dwellings because of the endless rains.
value.literal: An edict to Kaifeng Prefecture, because unending rains continued, ordered one month's rent remitted on public and private leased dwellings in the capital.

value.zh: 乙巳，詔安審琦率兵赴鄴都，皇甫遇赴相州。
value.en: On yisi An Shenqi was ordered to Ye and Huangfu Yu to Xiang.
value.literal: On yisi, an edict ordered An Shenqi to lead troops to Ye and Huangfu Yu to Xiang Prefecture.

value.zh: 丙午，以太子少保楊凝式為太子少傅，以刑部尚書王延為太子少保，前潁州團練使竇貞固為刑部尚書。
value.en: On bingwu Yang Ningshi became Senior Mentor, Wang Yan Junior Mentor, and former Ying commissioner Dou Zhengu Minister of Justice.
value.literal: On bingwu, Yang Ningshi, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Senior Mentor; Wang Yan, Minister of Justice, was made Junior Mentor; Dou Zhengu, former training commissioner of Ying Prefecture, was made Minister of Justice.

value.zh: 是月，河南、河北、關西諸州奏，大水霖雨不止，溝河泛濫，水入城郭及損害秋稼。
value.en: That month Henan, Hebei, and the western passes reported floods, endless rain, cities inundated, and crops ruined.
value.literal: That month Henan, Hebei, and the western passes reported that great floods and unending rains made ditches and rivers overflow, water entered cities, and the autumn grain was harmed.

value.zh: 是月，契丹瀛州刺史詐為書與樂壽將軍王巒，願以本城歸順，且言城中蕃軍不滿千人，請朝廷發軍襲取之，己為內應。
value.en: That month the Khitan prefect of Ying forged a letter to Leshou general Wang Luan offering surrender, claiming fewer than a thousand barbarian troops in the city and asking for a strike while he acted as insider.
value.literal: That month the Khitan prefect of Ying Prefecture forged a letter to Wang Luan, general of Leshou, offering to surrender the city and stating that barbarian troops in the city numbered fewer than a thousand, asking the court to send an army to seize it while he served as insider.

value.zh: 又云：「今秋苦雨，川澤漲溢，自瓦橋已北，水勢無際。
value.en: He also wrote: "This autumn's rains have flooded the rivers; north of Wagiao Bridge the waters are endless.
value.literal: He also wrote: "This autumn's bitter rains have made rivers and marshes overflow; from Wagiao Bridge northward the waters are boundless.

value.zh: 契丹已歸本國，若聞南夏有變，地遠阻水，雖欲奔命，無能及也。」
value.en: The Khitan have returned home; if they hear of trouble in the south, distance and flood would prevent any timely rescue."
value.literal: The Khitan have already returned to their own country; if they hear trouble in the Southern Court, the distance and the blocking waters mean that even if they wished to rush to the rescue, they could not arrive in time."

value.zh: 又，巒繼有密奏，苦言瀛、鄚可取之狀。
value.en: Wang Luan also sent secret memorials urgently arguing that Ying and Mo could be taken.
value.literal: Moreover Luan sent further secret memorials urgently arguing that Ying and Mo could be taken.

value.zh: 先是，前歲中車駕駐於河上，曾遣邊將遺書於幽州趙延壽，勸令歸國，延壽尋有報命，依違而已。
value.en: Earlier, when the emperor had been on the Yellow River, border generals wrote Zhao Yanshou at Youzhou urging return; his reply was evasive.
value.literal: Earlier, the year before when the imperial carriage was stationed on the Yellow River, border generals had been sent with letters to Zhao Yanshou at Youzhou urging him to return to the realm; Yanshou soon sent a reply, evasive and noncommittal.

value.zh: 是歲三月，復遣鄴都杜威致書於延壽，且述朝旨，啖以厚利，仍遣洺州軍將趙行實賫書而往，潛申款密。
value.en: That third month Du Wei of Ye again wrote Yanshou with court policy and rich inducements, sending Luozhou officer Zhao Xingshi with secret pledges.
value.literal: In the third month of this year Du Wei of Ye was again sent with a letter to Yanshou stating court policy, tempting him with rich rewards, and the Luozhou officer Zhao Xingshi was dispatched bearing the letter to convey secret pledges in private.

value.zh: 行實曾事延壽，故遣之。
value.en: Xingshi had once served Yanshou and was chosen for the mission.
value.literal: Xingshi had once served Yanshou, and therefore was sent.

value.zh: 七月，行實自燕回，得延壽書，且言：「久陷邊庭，願歸中國，乞發大軍應接，即拔身南去。」
value.en: In the seventh month Xingshi returned from Yan with Yanshou's letter: "Long trapped on the frontier, I wish to return to China; send a great army to meet me and I will come south at once."
value.literal: In the seventh month Xingshi returned from Yan with Yanshou's letter, which also stated: "Long trapped on the frontier, I wish to return to China; I beg that a great army be sent to meet me, and I will at once withdraw south."

value.zh: 敘致懇切，辭旨綿密，時朝廷欣然從之，復遣趙行實計會延壽大軍應接之所。
value.en: The tone was earnest; the court gladly agreed and again sent Zhao Xingshi to arrange the rendezvous.
value.literal: The tone was earnest and the wording close and careful; the court then gladly agreed and again sent Zhao Xingshi to arrange where Yanshou's great army should be met.

value.zh: 有瀛州大將遣所親賫蠟書至闕下，告雲欲謀翻變，以本城歸命。
value.en: A Ying general sent a sealed letter to court reporting a planned mutiny to surrender the city.
value.literal: A great general of Ying Prefecture sent a close associate bearing a sealed wax letter to the court reporting a planned mutiny to surrender the city.

value.zh: 未幾，會彼有告變者，事不果就。
value.en: Soon the plot was reported on the other side and came to nothing.
value.literal: Before long someone there reported the plot, and the affair did not succeed.

value.zh: 至是，瀛州守將劉延祚受契丹之命，詐輸誠款，以誘我軍，國家深以為信，遂有出師之議。
value.en: Now Ying commander Liu Yanzuo, on Khitan orders, feigned surrender to lure our army; the court believed him, and the campaign was launched.
value.literal: At this time Liu Yanzuo, the Ying garrison commander, on Khitan orders feigned sincere submission to lure our army; the state deeply trusted him, and therefore the debate to march troops arose.

value.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，諱榮，太祖之養子，蓋聖穆皇后之侄也。
value.en: Emperor Shizong, posthumously known as Ruiwu Xiaowen, bore the personal name Rong. He was Taizu's adopted son and a nephew of Empress Shengmu.
value.literal: The Emperor Shizong, posthumously titled Ruiwu Xiaowen, whose personal name was Rong, was the adopted son of Taizu and was in fact a nephew of Empress Shengmu.

value.zh: 本姓柴氏，父守禮，太子少保致仕。
value.en: He was born into the Chai family. His father Shouli had retired from the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: His original surname was the Chai clan; his father was Shouli, who had retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 〈（《隆平集》：柴翁者，嘗獨居室，人以為司冥事。
value.en: (According to the Longpingji, an elder of the Chai clan once lived alone in his room, and people believed he had dealings with the realm of the dead.
value.literal: (The Longpingji states: There was an Old Man Chai who once lived alone in his room, and people thought he dealt with matters of the underworld.

value.zh: 一日，笑不止，妻問其故，不答。
value.en: One day he could not stop laughing. When his wife asked why, he refused to say.
value.literal: One day he laughed without stopping; his wife asked the reason, but he would not answer.

value.zh: 翁嗜飲，妻醉之以酒，乃曰：「上帝有命，郭郎為天子。」
value.en: The old man loved wine, so his wife plied him with drink until he blurted out: "Heaven has decreed that Master Guo shall become emperor."
value.literal: The old man loved drink; his wife made him drunk with wine, and then he said: "Heaven has commanded that Master Guo shall become Son of Heaven."

value.zh: 考柴翁即守禮之父，史佚其名。）〉
value.en: It is held that this Old Man Chai was Shouli's father, though the history does not give his name.)〉
value.literal: Investigation shows that Old Man Chai was the father of Shouli; the history does not record his name.)〉

value.zh: 帝以唐天祐十八年，歲在辛巳，九月二十四日丙午，生於邢州之別墅。
value.en: He was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (bingwu) in Tianyou 18 of Tang (xinsi year), at a country estate in Xingzhou.
value.literal: The Emperor was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, bingwu, in the eighteenth year of Tang Tianyou, the year xinsi, at a villa in Xingzhou.

value.zh: 年未童冠，因侍聖穆皇后，在太祖左右。
value.en: While still a boy, he attended Empress Shengmu and remained close to Taizu.
value.literal: Before he had reached the age of the capping ceremony, he attended Empress Shengmu and was at Taizu's side.

value.zh: 時太祖無子，家道淪落，然以帝謹厚，故以庶事委之。
value.en: Taizu had no sons of his own, and the household had fallen on hard times, but he found the boy conscientious and dependable and began entrusting him with day-to-day affairs.
value.literal: At that time Taizu had no son, and the family's fortunes had declined; yet because the Emperor was careful and sincere, Taizu entrusted him with household affairs.

value.zh: 帝悉心經度，資用獲濟，太祖甚憐之，乃養為己子。
value.en: The boy managed everything with care, kept the household supplied, and won Taizu's deep affection; Taizu eventually adopted him as his son.
value.literal: The Emperor devoted himself to planning and management, and supplies were made adequate; Taizu cherished him greatly and therefore adopted him as his own son.

value.zh: 漢初，太祖以佐命功為樞密副使，帝始授左監門衛將軍。
value.en: Early in the Han dynasty Taizu became vice commissioner of military affairs for his founding service, and the future emperor received his first commission as general of the Left Gate Guards.
value.literal: At the beginning of Han, Taizu was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs for his merit in assisting the founding, and the Emperor was first appointed General of the Left Gate Guards.

value.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：周世宗在漢為諸衛將軍，嘗遊畿甸，謁縣令，忘其姓名，令方聚邑客蒱博，勿得見，世宗頗銜之。
value.en: (The Guolao tanyuan records that while serving as a general of the guards under Han, the future Zhou Shizong once toured the capital region and called on a county magistrate whose name is lost to us. The magistrate was hosting a gambling party for local guests and refused to see him, and Shizong never forgot the slight.
value.literal: (The Guolao tanyuan says: When Zhou Shizong was a general of the guards under Han, he once traveled in the capital region and called on a county magistrate, whose name is forgotten; the magistrate was just gathering local guests for gambling and would not receive him, and Shizong bore considerable resentment.

value.zh: 及即位，令因部夫犯贓數百匹，宰相範質以具獄上奏，世宗曰：「親民之官，贓狀狼籍，法當處死。」
value.en: After he took the throne, that same magistrate was implicated when laborers under his command embezzled hundreds of bolts of cloth. Chief minister Fan Zhi submitted the completed case. Shizong said, "An official charged with caring for the people, and his corruption this brazen—the law calls for death."
value.literal: When he acceded to the throne, that magistrate, because laborers under his command had embezzled several hundred bolts of cloth, had the full case submitted by the chief minister Fan Zhi; Shizong said: "An official close to the people, with corruption so flagrant—by law he should be put to death."

value.zh: 質奏曰：「受所監臨財物有罪，上贓雖多，法不至死。」
value.en: Fan Zhi replied, "Embezzling property under one's supervision is indeed a crime, but even with a large sum involved, the statute does not prescribe death."
value.literal: Fan Zhi memorialized: "Taking property under one's supervision is a crime, but though the amount embezzled is large, the law does not reach death."

value.zh: 世宗怒，厲聲曰：「法者自古帝王之所制，本以防奸，朕立法殺贓吏，非酷刑也。」
value.en: Shizong flared up and said sharply, "Law is what rulers have fashioned since antiquity to keep wrongdoing in check. When I use the law to execute corrupt officials, that is not cruelty."
value.literal: Shizong grew angry and said in a stern voice: "Law is what emperors and kings have made since antiquity, originally to guard against wrongdoing; that I make law to kill corrupt officials is not cruel punishment."

value.zh: 質曰：「陛下殺之則可，若付有司，臣不敢署敕。」
value.en: Fan Zhi said, "Your Majesty may execute him if you insist, but if the case goes through the regular judiciary, I cannot sign the edict."
value.literal: Fan Zhi said: "Your Majesty may kill him if you wish, but if the case is handed to the responsible offices, your servant dares not sign the edict."

value.zh: 遂貸其命。）〉
value.en: In the end his life was spared.)〉
value.literal: Thereupon his life was spared.)〉

value.zh: 二年，太祖鎮鄴，改天雄軍牙內都指揮使，領貴州刺史、檢校右僕射。
value.en: In the second year, when Taizu took command at Ye, he was made commander of the Tianxiong Army's inner guard, given Guizhou as his prefecture, and granted the honorary title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
value.literal: In year 2, when Taizu was stationed at Ye, he was changed to commander of the inner guard of the Tianxiong Army, and given charge of Guizhou as governor while serving as honorary Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

value.zh: 三年冬，太祖入平內難，留帝守鄴城。
value.en: That winter Taizu marched into the capital to settle the internal crisis and left him to hold Yecheng.
value.literal: In winter of year 3, when Taizu entered the capital to quell the internal crisis, he left the Emperor to guard Yecheng.

value.zh: 秋七月癸酉朔，前河西軍節度使申師厚責授右監門衛率府副率。
value.en: On the guiyou new moon of the seventh month of autumn, former Hexi military governor Shen Shihou was demoted to vice leader of the Right Gate Guards of the Supervisory Army.
value.literal: Autumn, seventh month, guiyou new moon, Shen Shihou, former military governor of the Hexi Army, was demoted and appointed Vice Leader of the Right Gate Guards of the Supervisory Army.

value.zh: 師厚在涼州歲餘，以所部艱食，蕃情反覆，奏乞入朝，尋留其子為留後，不俟詔離任，故責之。
value.en: Shihou had been at Liangzhou for more than a year. His troops lacked food and the tribes were unreliable, so he memorialized asking to come to court. He soon left his son as acting commissioner, left his post without awaiting an edict, and was punished for it.
value.literal: Shihou had been at Liangzhou for more than a year; because his command lacked food and the tribal disposition was inconstant, he memorialized begging to enter court; soon he left his son as acting commissioner without awaiting an edict and left his post—hence the punishment.

value.zh: 乙亥，天雄軍節度使、衛王府彥卿進位守太傅，改封魏王；
value.en: On yihai Tianxiong military governor and Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was advanced to Defender Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wei;
value.literal: On yihai, Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong Army and Prince of Wei, was advanced to Defender Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wei;

value.zh: 鄆州郭從義加兼中書令；
value.en: Yanzhou's Guo Congyi was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
value.literal: Guo Congyi of Yanzhou was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

value.zh: 河陽劉詞移鎮永興軍，加兼侍中；
value.en: Heyang's Liu Ci was transferred to Yongxing and additionally made palace attendant;
value.literal: Liu Ci of Heyang was transferred to the Yongxing Army and additionally made Palace Attendant;

value.zh: 潞州李筠加兼侍中；
value.en: Luzhou's Li Jun was additionally made palace attendant;
value.literal: Li Jun of Luzhou was additionally made Palace Attendant;

value.zh: 河中王彥超移鎮許州，加兼侍中；
value.en: Hezhong's Wang Yanchao was transferred to Xuzhou and additionally made palace attendant;
value.literal: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was transferred to Xuzhou and additionally made Palace Attendant;

value.zh: 許州節度、侍衛都虞候李重進移鎮宋州，加同平章事兼侍衛親軍都指揮使；
value.en: Xuzhou military governor and palace guard chief of staff Li Chongjin was transferred to Songzhou, made councilor, and appointed commander-in-chief of the imperial guard;
value.literal: Li Chongjin, military governor of Xuzhou and chief of staff of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou, made concurrent Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and appointed commander-in-chief of the imperial guard;

value.zh: 以武信軍節度使兼殿前都指揮使張永德為滑州節度使，加檢校太傅，典軍如故；
value.en: Wuxin military governor and Palace Front commander Zhang Yongde was made Huazhou military governor, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor, and kept army command as before;
value.literal: Zhang Yongde, military governor of the Wuxin Army and commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was made military governor of Huazhou, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor, and retained command of the army as before;

value.zh: 同州藥元福移鎮陜州，加檢校太尉；
value.en: Tongzhou's Yao Yuanfu was transferred to Shaanzhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;
value.literal: Yao Yuanfu of Tongzhou was transferred to Shaanzhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;

value.zh: 鄜州白重贊移鎮河陽，加檢校太尉；
value.en: Yongzhou's Bai Chongzan was transferred to Heyang and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;
value.literal: Bai Chongzan of Yongzhou was transferred to Heyang and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;

value.zh: 陜州韓通移鎮曹州，加檢校太傅。
value.en: Shaanzhou's Han Tong was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor.
value.literal: Han Tong of Shaanzhou was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor.

value.zh: 帝即位之初，覃慶於諸侯，是賞從征之功也。
value.en: At the beginning of his reign he had extended rewards widely to the feudal lords; this round rewarded those who had joined the campaign.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Emperor's accession he had bestowed rewards widely upon the feudal lords; this was to reward merit from the campaign.

value.zh: 丙子，以前禮部侍郎邊光範為刑部侍郎，權判開封府事。
value.en: On bingzi former Vice Minister of Rites Bian Guangfan was made Vice Minister of Justice and acting mayor of Kaifeng.
value.literal: On bingzi, Bian Guangfan, former Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice and acting mayor of Kaifeng.

value.zh: 丁丑，天下兵馬元帥、吳越國王錢俶加天下兵馬都元帥；
value.en: On dingchou Wu-Yue king and Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven Qian Chu was additionally made Marshal-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;
value.literal: On dingchou, Qian Chu, King of Wu-Yue and Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven, was additionally made Marshal-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;

value.zh: 襄州節度使、陳王安審琦加守太尉。
value.en: Xiangzhou military governor and Prince of Chen Wang Shenqi was advanced to Defender Grand Marshal.
value.literal: Wang Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou and Prince of Chen, was advanced to Defender Grand Marshal.

value.zh: 戊寅，右散騎常侍張可復卒。
value.en: On wuyin Right Regular Attendant Zhang Kefu died.
value.literal: On wuyin, Zhang Kefu, Right Regular Attendant, died.

value.zh: 以前亳州防禦使李萬金為鄜州留後。
value.en: Former Bozhou defense commissioner Li Wanjin was made acting commissioner of Yongzhou.
value.literal: Li Wanjin, former defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made acting commissioner of Yongzhou.

value.zh: 庚辰，幸南莊。
value.en: On gengchen the emperor visited the South Manor.
value.literal: On gengchen, the Emperor visited the South Manor.

value.zh: 辛巳，荊南節度使、南平王高保融加守中書令，夏州節度使、西平王李彜興加守太保，西京留守武行德、徐州王晏、鄧州侯章並加兼中書令。
value.en: On xinsi Jingnan military governor and Prince of Nanping Gao Baorong was advanced to Defender Councilor; Xiazhou military governor and Prince of Xiping Li Yixing was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde, Xuzhou's Wang Yan, and Dengzhou's Hou Zhang were all additionally made councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
value.literal: On xinsi, Gao Baorong, military governor of Jingnan and Prince of Nanping, was advanced to Defender Councilor; Li Yixing, military governor of Xiazhou and Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, Wang Yan of Xuzhou, and Hou Zhang of Dengzhou were all additionally made Councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

value.zh: 癸未，湖南王進逵加兼中書令；
value.en: On guimao Hunan's Wang Jinkui was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
value.literal: On guimao, Wang Jinkui of Hunan was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

value.zh: 天德軍節度使郭勛、邠州折從阮、安州李洪義並加兼侍中；
value.en: Tiande military governor Guo Xun, Binzhou's Zhe Congruan, and Anzhou's Li Hongyi were all additionally made palace attendants;
value.literal: Guo Xun, military governor of the Tiande Army, Zhe Congruan of Binzhou, and Li Hongyi of Anzhou were all additionally made Palace Attendants;

value.zh: 以前華州節度使孫方諫為同州節度使，加兼中書令；
