value.en: Former Hua military governor Sun Fangjian was appointed military governor of Tong and additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
value.literal: Previously Sun Fangjian, military governor of Hua, was made military governor of Tong, additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

value.zh: 以前永興軍節度使王仁鎬為河中節度使，加檢校太尉。
value.en: Former Yongxing military governor Wang Rengao was appointed military governor of Hezhong and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.
value.literal: Previously Wang Rengao, military governor of the Yongxing Army, was made military governor of Hezhong, promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.

value.zh: 乙酉，滄州李暉、貝州王饒、鎮州曹英並加兼侍中，涇州張鐸、相州王進、延州袁鳷並加檢校太尉。
value.en: On yiyou Cangzhou's Li Hui, Beizhou's Wang Rao, and Zhenzhou's Cao Ying were all additionally made palace attendants; Jingzhou's Zhang Duo, Xiangzhou's Wang Jin, and Yanzhou's Yuan Zhi were all promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.
value.literal: On yiyou, Li Hui of Cangzhou, Wang Rao of Beizhou, and Cao Ying of Zhenzhou were all additionally made Palace Attendants; Zhang Duo of Jingzhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Yuan Zhi of Yanzhou were all promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.

value.zh: 壬辰，百僚上表，請以九月二十四日誕聖日為天清節，從之。
value.en: On renchen the officials memorialized to make the emperor's birthday, the twenty-fourth of the ninth month, the Tianqing Festival. The request was granted.
value.literal: On renchen, the hundred officials submitted a memorial requesting that the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day of the sage's birth, be established as the Tianqing Festival; it was approved.

value.zh: 癸巳，以左僕射兼門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史範質為守司徒兼門下侍郎、平章事、宏文館大學士；
value.en: On guisi Left Vice Minister, Secretariat Chamberlain, councilor, and supervisor of state history Fan Zhi was advanced to Defender Grand Mentor, retaining his posts as Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, and made Grandee of the Hongwen Academy;
value.literal: On guisi, Fan Zhi, Left Vice Minister concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of state history, was made Defender Grand Mentor concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and Grandee of the Hongwen Academy;

value.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：周太祖嘗令世宗詣範質，時為親王，軒車高大，門不能容，世宗即下馬步入。
value.en: (The Guolao Tanyuan records that Zhou Taizu once sent Shizong to visit Fan Zhi when the latter was still a prince. Shizong's carriage was so tall the gate would not take it, so he dismounted and entered on foot.
value.literal: (The 《Guolao Tanyuan》 states: Zhou Taizu once had Shizong go to Fan Zhi's residence; he was then a prince. His carriage was tall and the gate could not admit it; Shizong at once dismounted and walked in on foot.

value.zh: 及嗣位，從容語質曰：「卿所居舊宅耶，門樓一何小哉。」
value.en: After he took the throne, he said to Fan Zhi with easy familiarity, "Is this your old house? What a tiny gate-tower!"
value.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, he said to Fan Zhi in an easy manner: "Is this the old residence in which you dwell? How very small the gate-tower is!"

value.zh: 遂為治第。）〉
value.en: He then had a new residence built for him.)〉
value.literal: Thereupon a mansion was built for him.)〉

value.zh: 以左僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士、判三司李穀為守司徒兼門下侍朗、平章事，監修國史；
value.en: Left Vice Minister, Secretariat Chamberlain, councilor, Jixian Hall Grandee, and overseer of the Three Offices Li Gu was advanced to Defender Grand Mentor, retaining his posts as Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, and made supervisor of state history;
value.literal: Li Gu, Left Vice Minister concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, Jixian Hall Grandee, and overseer of the Three Offices, was made Defender Grand Mentor concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of state history;

value.zh: 以中書侍郎、平章事王溥為中書侍郎兼禮部尚書、平章事、集賢殿大學士；
value.en: Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor Wang Pu was made Secretariat Chamberlain and Minister of Rites, councilor, and Jixian Hall Grandee;
value.literal: Wang Pu, Secretariat Chamberlain and Councilor, was made Secretariat Chamberlain concurrently Minister of Rites, Councilor, and Jixian Hall Grandee;

value.zh: 以樞密院學士、工部侍郎景範為中書侍郎、平章事，判三司；
value.en: Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works Jing Fan was made Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, with charge of the Three Offices;
value.literal: Jing Fan, Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works, was made Secretariat Chamberlain and Councilor, overseeing the Three Offices;

value.zh: 樞密使、檢校太保、同平章事鄭仁誨加兼侍中；
value.en: Privy Commissioner, Honorary Grand Guardian, and concurrent councilor Zheng Renhui was additionally made palace attendant;
value.literal: Zheng Renhui, Privy Commissioner, Honorary Grand Guardian, and Concurrent Councilor, was additionally made Palace Attendant;

value.zh: 靈武馮繼業、定州孫行友、邢州田景鹹並加檢校太傅；
value.en: Lingwu's Feng Jiye, Dingzhou's Sun Xingyou, and Xingzhou's Tian Jingxian were all promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor;
value.literal: Feng Jiye of Lingwu, Sun Xingyou of Dingzhou, and Tian Jingxian of Xingzhou were all promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor;

value.zh: 晉州楊廷璋加檢校太保；
value.en: Jinzhou's Yang Tingzhang was promoted to Honorary Grand Guardian;
value.literal: Yang Tingzhang of Jinzhou was promoted to Honorary Grand Guardian;

value.zh: 以太子詹事趙上交為太子賓客。
value.en: Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Zhao Shangjiao was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: Zhao Shangjiao, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 乙未，以樞密副使、右監門衛大將軍魏仁浦為樞密使、檢校太保。
value.en: On yiwei Deputy Privy Commissioner and Right Imperial Insignia Guard Major General Wei Renpu was made Privy Commissioner and Honorary Grand Guardian.
value.literal: On yiwei, Wei Renpu, Deputy Privy Commissioner and Major General of the Right Imperial Insignia Guard, was made Privy Commissioner and Honorary Grand Guardian.

value.zh: 〈（《東都事略》云：議者以仁浦不由科第進，世宗曰：「顧才何如耳！」
value.en: (The Dongdu Shilue records that critics objected that Renpu had not risen through the examination system. Shizong replied, "What matters is ability, does it not!"
value.literal: (The 《Dongdu Shilue》 states: Discussants held that Renpu had not advanced through the civil service examinations. Shizong said: "What matters is talent, does it not!"

value.zh: 遂用之。）〉
value.en: He was appointed.)〉
value.literal: Thereupon he was appointed.)〉

value.zh: 丙申，以中書舍人史館修撰、判館事劉溫叟為禮部侍郎，判館如故。
value.en: On bingshen Secretariat Drafter, History Bureau compiler, and bureau director Liu Wen'ou was made Vice Minister of Rites while retaining his bureau duties.
value.literal: On bingshen, Liu Wen'ou, Secretariat Drafter, History Bureau compiler, and director of the bureau, was made Vice Minister of Rites; his duties at the bureau remained as before.

value.zh: 丁酉，相州節度使王進卒。
value.en: On dingyou Xiangzhou military governor Wang Jin died.
value.literal: On dingyou, Wang Jin, military governor of Xiangzhou, died.

value.zh: 冬十月甲辰，左羽林大將軍孟漢卿賜死，坐監納厚取耗餘也。
value.en: In the tenth month of winter, on jiachen Left Feathered Forest Major General Meng Hanqing was ordered to take his own life for skimming excess grain while supervising tax collection.
value.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, Meng Hanqing, Major General of the Left Feathered Forest, was granted death for supervising collection and taking a heavy surplus in collection.

value.zh: 丙午，以安州節度使李洪義為青州節度使，以貝州節度使王饒為相州節度使，以徐州節度使王晏為西京留守，以西京留守武行德為徐州節度使。
value.en: On bingwu Anzhou military governor Li Hongyi was moved to Qingzhou; Beizhou military governor Wang Rao to Xiangzhou; Xuzhou military governor Wang Yan to Western Capital defender; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde to Xuzhou military governor.
value.literal: On bingwu, Li Hongyi, military governor of Anzhou, was made military governor of Qingzhou; Wang Rao, military governor of Beizhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou; Wang Yan, military governor of Xuzhou, was made Western Capital resident defender; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, was made military governor of Xuzhou.

value.zh: 戊申，以龍捷左廂都指揮使、泗州防禦使韓令坤為洋州節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使；
value.en: On wushen Dragon Swift Left Wing commander and Sizhou defense commissioner Han Lingkun was made Yangzhou military governor and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry;
value.literal: On wushen, Han Lingkun, commander of the Dragon Swift Left Wing and defense commissioner of Sizhou, was made military governor of Yangzhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry;

value.zh: 以虎捷右廂都指揮使、永州防禦使李繼勛為利州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使。
value.en: Tiger Swift Right Wing commander and Yongzhou defense commissioner Li Jixun was made Lizhou military governor and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard infantry.
value.literal: Li Jixun, commander of the Tiger Swift Right Wing and defense commissioner of Yongzhou, was made military governor of Lizhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard infantry.

value.zh: 己酉，太子太保致仕楊凝式卒。
value.en: On jiyou retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yang Ningshi died.
value.literal: On jiyou, Yang Ningshi, retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, died.

value.zh: 詔安、貝二州依舊為防禦州，其軍額並停。
value.en: An edict restored An and Bei to defense prefectures as before and abolished their military designations.
value.literal: An edict restored An and Bei prefectures to defense prefectures as before; their army designations were all abolished.

value.zh: 壬子，以今上為永州防禦使，依前殿前都虞候。
value.en: On renzi the present sovereign was made Yongzhou defense commissioner while retaining his post as chief of staff of the Palace Front Division.
value.literal: On renzi, the present sovereign was made defense commissioner of Yongzhou, retaining his former post as chief of staff of the Palace Front Division.

value.zh: 戊午，監修國史李穀等上言曰：「竊以自古王者鹹建史官，君臣獻替之謀皆須備載，家國安危之道得以直書。
value.en: On wuwu Li Gu and the other supervisors of state history submitted a memorial: "We observe that since antiquity every conquering sovereign has established historiographers, so that counsel offered and withdrawn between ruler and minister might all be fully recorded and the paths of national safety and peril written without distortion.
value.literal: On wuwu, Li Gu and others, supervisors of the compilation of state history, submitted saying: "We venture to observe that since antiquity conquering kings have all established historiographers; the counsel of ruler and minister, whether offered or withdrawn, must all be fully recorded, and the paths of the state's safety and peril can thereby be written straight.

value.zh: 歷代已來，其名不一。
value.en: Through the ages their titles have varied.
value.literal: Through the generations their titles have not been uniform.

value.zh: 人君言動，則起居註創於累朝；
value.en: The ruler's words and deeds were recorded in the Diaries of Activity and Repose, instituted dynasty after dynasty;
value.literal: For the ruler's words and deeds there is the Diaries of Activity and Repose, instituted across successive reigns;

value.zh: 輔相經綸，則時政記興於前代。
value.en: the chancellor's governance in the Record of Current Administration, which arose in earlier times.
value.literal: for the chancellor's governance, the Record of Current Administration arose in former ages.

value.zh: 然後采其事實，編作史書。
value.en: Only then were the facts gathered and compiled into formal histories.
value.literal: Only then were the facts gathered and compiled into historical books.

value.zh: 蓋緣聞見之間須有來處，記錄之際得以審詳。
value.en: This was because what the historians heard and saw had to come from somewhere, so that what they recorded could be thorough and exact.
value.literal: This was because between what was heard and seen there had to be a source, and at the time of recording one could be thorough and exact.

value.zh: 今之左右起居郎，即古之左右史也。
value.en: Today's Left and Right Diarists are the ancient Left and Right Historians.
value.literal: Today's Left and Right Diarists are the ancient Left and Right Historians.

value.zh: 唐文宗朝，命其官執筆，立於殿階螭頭之下，以紀政事。
value.en: Under Tang Wenzong these officers were ordered to take up their brushes and stand below the dragon-head steps of the throne hall to record affairs of state.
value.literal: In the reign of Tang Wenzong, these officers were ordered to hold the brush and stand below the dragon-head steps of the hall to record government affairs.

value.zh: 後則明宗朝，命端明殿及樞密直學士，皆輪修日曆，旋送史官，以備纂修。
value.en: Later, under Mingzong, Duanming Hall scholars and Privy Council direct academicians were ordered to compile the court calendar in rotation and send it promptly to the historiographers for use in compilation.
value.literal: Later, in the reign of Mingzong, the Duanming Hall and direct academicians of the Privy Council were all ordered to take turns compiling the court calendar, which was promptly sent to the historiographers to supply material for compilation.

value.zh: 及近朝，此事皆廢，史官惟憑百司報狀，館司但取兩省制書，此外雖有訪聞，例非端的。
value.en: In recent times this practice had been abandoned entirely. Historiographers relied only on reports from the ministries, and the History Bureau took only edicts from the two secretariats. Whatever else they heard was, as a rule, unreliable.
value.literal: By recent times this practice had all been abandoned; historiographers relied only on reports from the hundred offices, and the institute took only edicts from the two secretariats; beyond this, though there might be inquiries and hearsay, as a rule it was not reliable.

value.zh: 伏自先皇帝創開昌運，及皇帝陛下纘嗣丕基，其聖德武功、神謀睿略，而皆萬幾宥密，丹禁深嚴，非外臣之所知，豈庶僚之可訪。
value.en: Since the late emperor opened this flourishing age and Your Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation, his sagely virtue, martial achievement, divine stratagems, and keen plans all lie within the myriad affairs of the inner court, deep within the vermilion forbidden precincts. These are not matters outer ministers can know, nor subjects common officials may inquire into.
value.literal: We bow before the fact that the late emperor opened a flourishing age, and Your Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation; his sagely virtue and martial achievement, divine stratagems and keen plans—all lie within the myriad affairs of the inner court, deep and secret within the vermilion forbidden precincts, not what outer ministers can know, how could common officials be consulted?

value.zh: 此後欲望以諮詢之事、裁制之規，別命近臣旋具抄錄，每當修撰日曆，即令封付史臣，庶國事無漏略之文，職業免疏遺之咎。」
value.en: Henceforth we ask that matters of consultation and rules of decision be specially entrusted to nearby ministers to copy at once, and that whenever the court calendar is compiled these copies be sealed and delivered to the historiographers, so that state affairs suffer no omissions and the historiographers escape the charge of negligence."
value.literal: Hereafter we desire that on matters of consultation and rules of decision special orders be given to nearby ministers to prepare copies at once; whenever the court calendar is compiled, let these be sealed and delivered to the historiographers, so that state affairs may have no omitted passages and the profession may escape the fault of negligence."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The memorial was approved.
value.literal: It was approved.

value.zh: 因命樞密直學士，起今後於樞密使處，逐月抄錄事件，送付史館。
value.en: Privy Council direct academicians were accordingly ordered, beginning immediately, to copy monthly from the Privy Commissioner's records and deliver the copies to the History Bureau.
value.literal: Accordingly Privy Council direct academicians were ordered, beginning from now at the Privy Commissioner's office, to copy events month by month and send them to the History Bureau.

value.zh: 己未，供奉官郝光庭棄市，坐在葉縣巡檢日，挾私斷殺平人也。
value.en: On jiwei palace service official Hao Guangting was executed in the marketplace for killing a commoner in a private judgment while serving as patrol inspector of Ye County.
value.literal: On jiwei, Hao Guangting, palace service official, was executed in the marketplace for, while serving as patrol inspector of Ye County, killing a commoner in a private judgment.

value.zh: 是日大閱，帝親臨之。
value.en: That day a grand military review was held, and the emperor attended in person.
value.literal: That day there was a great review; the emperor personally attended it.

value.zh: 帝自高平之役，睹諸軍未甚嚴整，遂有退卻，至是命今上一概簡閱，選武藝超絕者，署為殿前諸班，因是有散員、散指揮使、內殿直、散都頭、鐵騎、控鶴之號。
value.en: Since Gaoping the emperor had seen how poorly disciplined the armies were and how readily they fell back. He now ordered the present sovereign to review them all, selecting men of outstanding martial skill for the various companies of the Palace Front. Hence came the designations Loose Companies, Loose Commanders, Inner Hall Direct, Loose Squad Chiefs, Iron Cavalry, and Crane Control.
value.literal: Since the campaign at Gaoping the emperor had seen that the various armies were not very strict and orderly and had withdrawn; at this time he ordered the present sovereign to review them all comprehensively, selecting those of surpassing martial skill and appointing them to the various companies of the Palace Front; hence there came to be the designations Loose Companies, Loose Commanders, Inner Hall Direct, Loose Squad Chiefs, Iron Cavalry, and Crane Control.

value.zh: 復命總戎者，自龍捷、虎捷以降，一一選之，老弱羸小者去之，諸軍士伍，無不精當。
value.en: He also ordered the army commanders, from Dragon Swift and Tiger Swift downward, to inspect their troops one by one, removing the old, weak, and stunted until every company in every army was fit and exact.
value.literal: He again ordered the commanders-in-chief, from Dragon Swift and Tiger Swift downward, to select one by one; the old, weak, emaciated, and small were removed, and in every army company nothing was not exact and proper.

value.zh: 由是兵甲之盛，近代無比，且減冗食之費焉。
value.en: The army's arms and armor were thereafter unmatched in recent memory, and the cost of feeding useless mouths was reduced as well.
value.literal: By this the abundance of arms and armor had no parallel in recent times, and moreover superfluous consumption of provisions was reduced.

value.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：顯德元年，上謂侍臣曰：「侍衛兵士老少相半，強懦不分，蓋徇人情，不能選練。
value.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties records that in the first year of Xiande the emperor told his ministers, "Our palace guards are half old men and half young, with no distinction between the strong and the weak. We indulge personal ties and cannot drill them properly.
value.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》: In the first year of Xiande, the emperor said to his attending ministers: "The palace guard soldiers are half old and half young, strong and weak undistinguished; this indulges personal feeling and cannot select and drill.

value.zh: 今春朕在高平，與劉崇及蕃軍相遇，臨敵有指使不前者，茍非朕親當堅陣，幾至喪敗。
value.en: This spring at Gaoping I met Liu Chong and the Khitan army. Some of my officers would not advance when ordered. Had I not personally held the line, we would nearly have been destroyed.
value.literal: This spring I was at Gaoping and met Liu Chong and the barbarian army; facing the enemy there were those under command who would not advance; if I had not personally taken the firm line, we would nearly have suffered defeat.

value.zh: 況百戶農夫，未能贍一甲士，且兵在精不在眾，宜令一一點選，精銳者升在上軍，怯懦者任從安便，庶期可用，又不虛費。」
value.en: A hundred farming households cannot even support one armored soldier. Soldiers depend on quality, not numbers. Each man should be inspected: the elite raised into the upper armies, the timid allowed to go where they will, so that what we keep is useful and nothing is wasted."
value.literal: Moreover, a hundred farming households cannot support one armored soldier; moreover, in soldiers quality matters, not numbers; it is fitting to order selection one by one—the sharp and elite to be raised into the upper armies, the timid and weak allowed to go where they please, so that we may expect usefulness and not waste in vain."

value.zh: 先是，上按於高平，觀其退縮，慨然有懲革之志。
value.en: Earlier, when he inspected the troops at Gaoping and watched them fall back, he had resolved to reform them.
value.literal: Earlier, when the emperor inspected at Gaoping and saw them withdraw, he sighed and had the will to punish and reform.

value.zh: 又以驍勇之士，多為外諸侯所占，如是召募天下豪傑，不以草澤為阻，在於闕下，躬親試閱，選武藝超絕及有身首者，分署為殿前諸班。）〉
value.en: Bold warriors had also been snapped up by regional lords, so he recruited heroes from across the realm without regard to humble birth. At court he personally tested them, selecting men of outstanding skill and imposing stature for the various companies of the Palace Front.)〉
value.literal: Moreover, because bold and brave men were mostly taken by outer feudal lords, he therefore recruited heroes throughout the empire, not obstructed by commoners in the wilds; at the court he personally tested and reviewed them, selecting those of surpassing martial skill and of stature, and assigning them in divisions to the various companies of the Palace Front.)〉

value.zh: 淮河泇河衛河漳河沁河滹沱河桑乾河膠萊河
value.en: The Huai River; the Jia River; the Wei River; the Zhang River; the Qin River; the Hutuo River; the Sanggan River; the Jiao-Lai River.
value.literal: Huai River, Jia River, Wei River, Zhang River, Qin River, Hutuo River, Sanggan River, Jiao-Lai River.

value.zh: 明年，清復言：「東南漕舟，水淺弗能進。
value.en: The next year Liu Qing spoke again: "The grain ships from the southeast cannot advance because the water is too shallow.
value.literal: Next year, Qing again said: "Southeast grain transport boats, water shallow cannot advance.

value.zh: 請自滎澤入沁河，浚岡頭百二十里以通衛河。
value.en: I ask that they enter the Qin from Xingze, dredge one hundred and twenty li at Gangtou to link with the Wei River.
value.literal: Request from Xingze enter Qin River, dredge Gangtou one hundred twenty li to connect Wei River.

value.zh: 且張秋之決，由沁合黃，勢遂奔急。
value.en: Moreover, the breach at Zhangqiu came from the Qin joining the Yellow River, and the current became swift and violent.
value.literal: Moreover Zhangqiu's breach, because Qin joined Yellow, momentum then rushed urgent.

value.zh: 若引沁入衛，則張秋無患。」
value.en: If the Qin were led into the Wei, Zhangqiu would be spared further trouble."
value.literal: If lead Qin enter Wei, then Zhangqiu no worry."

value.zh: 行人王晏亦言：「開岡頭置閘，分沁水，使南入黃，北達衛。
value.en: Courier Wang Yan also said: "Open Gangtou and install locks to divide the Qin so that one branch flows south into the Yellow River and another north to the Wei.
value.literal: Courier Wang Yan also said: "Open Gangtou place locks, divide Qin water, make south enter Yellow, north reach Wei.

value.zh: 遇漲則閉閘，漕可永無患。」
value.en: When the waters rise, close the locks, and the grain transport will never again be in danger."
value.literal: Encounter flood then close locks, grain transport can forever no worry."

value.zh: 並下督漕都御史王竑等核實以聞。
value.en: Both proposals were forwarded to Wang Hong, the supervising censor-in-chief of grain transport, and others for verification and report.
value.literal: Both sent down to grain transport supervising censor-in-chief Wang Hong and others verify facts to report.

value.zh: 明年，給事中何升言：「沁河有漏港已成河。
value.en: The next year, Supervising Secretary He Sheng said: "On the Qin there is a leaking port that has already formed a full channel.
value.literal: Next year, supervising secretary He Sheng said: "Qin River has leaking harbor already become river.

value.zh: 臨清屯聚膠淺之舟，宜使從此入黃，度二旬可達淮。」
value.en: The boats stalled in shallow water at Linqing should be sent through it into the Yellow River; in about twenty days they could reach the Huai."
value.literal: Linqing gathered stuck shallow boats, should make them from here enter Yellow, estimate twenty days can reach Huai."

value.zh: 詔竑及都御史徐有貞閱之。
value.en: The emperor ordered Wang Hong and Censor-in-Chief Xu Youzhen to inspect the site.
value.literal: Edict Wang Hong and censor-in-chief Xu Youzhen inspect it.

value.zh: 既而罷引沁河議。
value.en: Soon afterward the plan to divert the Qin was dropped.
value.literal: Soon after abandoned draw Qin River proposal.

value.zh: 初，王晏請漕沁，有司多言弗利。
value.en: At first, when Wang Yan proposed using the Qin for grain transport, many local officers said it would not pay.
value.literal: Initially, Wang Yan requested grain transport Qin, responsible officials many spoke not advantageous.

value.zh: 晏固爭。
value.en: Wang Yan pressed his case stubbornly.
value.literal: Yan firmly contended.

value.zh: 吏部尚書王直請遣官行河，命侍郎趙榮同晏往。
value.en: Minister Wang Zhi of the Ministry of Personnel asked that officials be sent to survey the river, and Vice Minister Zhao Rong was ordered to go with Wang Yan.
value.literal: Ministry of Personnel Minister Wang Zhi requested send officials travel river, ordered Vice Minister Zhao Rong together with Yan go.

value.zh: 榮亦言不利，議乃寢。
value.en: Zhao Rong also reported that it would not work, and the plan was shelved.
value.literal: Rong also spoke not advantageous, proposal then shelved.

value.zh: 天順八年，都察院都事金景輝復請浚陳橋集古河，分引沁水，北通長垣、曹州、鉅野，以達漕河。
value.en: In the eighth year of Tianshun, Clerk Jin Jinghui of the Censorate again asked to dredge the Jigu River at Chenqiao, divide off part of the Qin, link it north through Changyuan, Caozhou, and Juye to the grain-transport canal.
value.literal: Tianshun eighth year, Censorate clerk Jin Jinghui again requested dredge Chenqiao Jigu River, divide draw Qin water, north connect Changyuan, Caozhou, Juye, to reach grain transport river.

value.zh: 詔按實以聞，未能行也。
value.en: An edict ordered verification and report, but it could not be carried out.
value.literal: Edict verify facts to report, unable carry out also.

value.zh: 南齊書卷二十三‧列傳第四
value.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4
value.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4

value.zh: 頃之寢疾。
value.en: Before long he fell gravely ill.
value.literal: Before long he took to his bed with illness.

value.zh: 上相星連有變，淵憂之，表遜位。
value.en: The Superior Minister star showed linked disturbances; troubled, Yuan memorialized to yield his post.
value.literal: The Superior Minister star showed linked changes; Yuan was troubled and memorialized to yield his post.

value.zh: 又因王儉及侍中王晏口陳於世祖，世祖不許。
value.en: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan plead in person before Shizu; Shizu refused.
value.literal: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan speak orally before Shizu; Shizu did not consent.

value.zh: 又啓曰：「臣顧惟凡薄，福過災生，未能以正情自安，遠慚彥輔。
value.en: He wrote again: "Your servant knows himself common and slight—favor has outstripped desert and trouble follows; I cannot quiet my heart in truth and am ashamed before worthy counselors.
value.literal: He memorialized again, saying, "Your servant reflects on his common mediocrity—blessing has outrun merit and calamity is born; unable to settle his heart in rectitude, far ashamed before worthy counselors.

value.zh: 旣內懷耿介，便覺晷刻難推。
value.en: Outward duty sits ill on an inward stiffness; hour by hour drags.
value.literal: Inwardly unyielding, each instant becomes hard to bear.

value.zh: 叨職未久，首歲便嬰疾篤，爾來沈痼，頻經危殆，彌深憂震。
value.en: I have not long held office; in the first year I was stricken gravely ill; since then lingering sickness, again and again at death's door, and dread only deepens.
value.literal: Your servant bore office not long; in the first year he fell gravely ill; since then chronic ailments, passing danger again and again, worry and dread ever deeper.

value.zh: 陛下曲存遲回，或謂僉議同異，此出於留慈每過，愛欲其榮。
value.en: Your Majesty has indulged my delay, or some will say the councils are divided—but this is only excess of kindness, love wishing me honor I do not merit.
value.literal: Your Majesty bent to allow delay; some say the collective deliberations differ—this comes from lingering affection exceeding measure, love wishing him honor.

value.zh: 臣年四十有八，叨忝若此，以疾陳遜，豈駭聽察。
value.en: At forty-eight, with honors heaped on me, to plead illness and withdraw—would that shock your ears?
value.literal: Your servant is forty-eight, bearing such honor at fault; to cite illness and yield—is that to startle imperial hearing?

value.zh: 總錄之任，江左罕授，上隣亞台，升降蓋微。
value.en: The overall Recordership is rarely granted in our age; its holder stands next to the Secretariat itself, and between rise and fall there is little distance.
value.literal: The charge of overall recording is rarely granted south of the Yangtze; it borders the secondary terrace, promotion and demotion scarcely distinct.

value.zh: 今受祿弗辭，退絀斯願，於臣名器，非曰貶少，萬物耳目，皎然共見，寧足仰延聖慮，稍垂矜惜。
value.en: To keep the stipend and refuse to step down, to choke off this request—for my name and rank that is no real demotion; every eye under heaven sees it plain. Why should it draw your concern or the least pity?
value.literal: Now to accept salary without declining, to withdraw and cut short this wish—for your servant's name and rank it is not called a belittling reduction; all eyes under heaven see it clearly—how could it merit extending imperial concern or slight pity?

value.zh: 臣若內飾廉譽，外循謙後，此則憲書行劾，刑綱是肅。
value.en: If I papered myself with a show of integrity while playing at humility, the statutes would impeach me and the law would tighten its net.
value.literal: If your servant adorned himself inwardly with reputation for integrity and outwardly followed humility, then the statutes would move to impeachment and the penal net would be tightened.

value.zh: 臣赤誠不能行，亦幽明所不宥。
value.en: My naked heart cannot do that; neither the living nor the dead would forgive it.
value.literal: Your servant's naked sincerity cannot perform that; neither the visible nor invisible worlds would pardon it.

value.zh: 區區寸心，歸啓以實。
value.en: In this inch of heart I lay the truth before you.
value.literal: This paltry inch of heart returns to declare in truth.

value.zh: 自吝寸陰，寔願方倍堯世。
value.en: Grudging every inch of daylight, I would only wish to serve twice the years of Yao's age.
value.literal: Cherishing each inch of shadow, truly wishing to match doubled the era of Yao.

value.zh: 昔王弘固請，乃於司徒爲衞將軍，宋氏行之不疑，當時物無異議，以臣方之，曾何足說。
value.en: Wang Hong once pressed his plea and was made Defender-General under the Minister of Works; the Song court granted it without a murmur. Set beside me, what is my case worth speaking of?
value.literal: Formerly Wang Hong firmly petitioned and became Defender-General under the Minister of Works; the Song house did it without doubt and none objected—compared with your servant, how could words suffice?

value.zh: 伏願恢闡宏猷，賜開亭造，則臣死之日，猶生之年。」
value.en: I beg you to widen your great design and grant me leave; then the day I die would still count as a day I lived."
value.literal: Bowing head, hoping to broaden great design, grant opening and release—then the day of your servant's death would still be as a day of life."

value.zh: 乃改授司空，領驃騎將軍，侍中、錄尚書如故。
value.en: He was then reassigned Minister of Works, retaining Supernal General, Palace Attendant, and Recorder as before.
value.literal: He was then reassigned Minister of Works, with Supernal General, Palace Attendant and Recorder unchanged.

value.zh: 上遣侍中王晏黃門郎王秀之問疾。
value.en: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to ask after his health.
value.literal: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to inquire after his illness.

value.zh: 薨，家無餘財，負債至數十萬。
value.en: He died; the family left no surplus, and debts ran into the hundreds of thousands.
value.literal: He died; the household had no surplus wealth, debts running to hundreds of thousands.

value.zh: 詔曰：「司徒奄至薨逝，痛怛慟懷，比雖尪瘵，便力出臨哭。
value.en: An edict read, "The Minister of Works has suddenly died; grief wounds the heart. Though lately I have been ill and frail, I went myself to mourn at his bier.
value.literal: An edict said, "The Minister of Works suddenly reached death's end; grief and anguish pierce the heart. Though lately wasting ill, I went in person to mourn at his bier.

value.zh: 給東園祕器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢二十萬，布二百疋，蠟二百斤。」
value.en: Grant eastern-garden funerary coffinware, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, two hundred thousand in cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax."
value.literal: Granted eastern garden secret coffinware, one set court robes, one suit of clothing, two hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts cloth, two hundred jin wax."

value.zh: 其年疾，上親臨視，薨，年三十八。
value.en: That year he sickened; the emperor came in person to his bedside. He died at thirty-eight.
value.literal: That year he fell ill; the emperor personally visited him. He died, aged thirty-eight.

value.zh: 吏部尚書王晏啓及儉喪，上答曰：「儉年德富盛，志用方隆，豈意暴疾，不展救護，便爲異世，奄忽如此，痛酷彌深。
value.en: Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel, wrote on Jian's death. The emperor answered: "Jian's years and virtue stood at their height, his will and work just ascending—who could have thought a sudden sickness, with no room for cure, would cast him so quickly into another world? The pain cuts unbearably deep.
value.literal: Wang Yan, Minister of the Masters of Personnel, memorialized on Jian's death. The emperor replied, "Jian's years and virtue were in fullest flower, his ambition and use just rising—who could have thought a sudden illness, with no scope for healing, would place him in another world so abruptly? The pain is unbearably deep.

value.zh: 其契闊艱運，義重常懷，言尋悲切，不能自勝。
value.en: His shared trials through hard times, the weight of right feeling I always bore—to speak of it is grief I cannot hold in.
value.literal: His trials through hard fates, his constant weight of right feeling—to speak of them is grief that cuts; I cannot master myself.

value.zh: 痛矣奈何！
value.en: Pain—what can be done!
value.literal: Pain—what can be done!

value.zh: 往矣奈何！」
value.en: Gone—what can be done!"
value.literal: Gone—what can be done!"

value.zh: 詔衞軍文武及臺所兵仗可悉停待葬。
value.en: An edict ordered all civil and military staff of the Guard General and all arms of the central offices to stand idle until the burial.
value.literal: Edict: All civil and military officers of the Guard General and all central-office arms and equipment shall halt until the burial.

value.zh: 蕭景先
value.en: Xiao Jingxian
value.literal: Xiao Jingxian

value.zh: 子毅，以勳戚子，少歷清官。
value.en: His son Yi, as the son of a meritorious kinsman, early held respectable posts.
value.literal: His son Yi, as son of a meritorious kinsman, in youth passed through pure offices.

value.zh: 太子舍人，洗馬，隨王友，永嘉太守，大司馬諮議參軍，南康太守，中書郎。
value.en: He served as Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, Friend of the Prince of Sui, Administrator of Yongjia, Adviser on the staff of the Grand Marshal, Administrator of Nankang, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
value.literal: Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, Friend of the Prince of Sui, Administrator of Yongjia, Adviser of the Grand Marshal, Administrator of Nankang, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

value.zh: 建武初，爲撫軍司馬，遷北中郎司馬。
value.en: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was Marshal of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters, then Marshal of the North Central Commandant headquarters.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was Marshal of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters and was transferred to Marshal of the North Central Commandant headquarters.

value.zh: 虜動，領軍守琅邪城。
value.en: When the northerners moved, he commanded troops in the defense of Langye.
value.literal: When the barbarians stirred, he led the army in defending Langye city.

value.zh: 毅性奢豪，好弓馬，爲高宗所疑忌。
value.en: Yi was extravagant by nature and loved archery and horsemanship; Emperor Ming came to view him with suspicion.
value.literal: Yi's nature was extravagant and proud; he loved bow and horse and was suspected and envied by Emperor Ming.

value.zh: 王晏事敗，幷陷誅之。
value.en: When Wang Yan's plot failed, Yi was implicated and executed along with him.
value.literal: When Wang Yan's affair failed, Yi was implicated and executed with him.

value.zh: 遣軍圍宅，毅時會賔客奏伎，聞變，索刀未得，收人突進，挾持毅入與母別，出便殺之。
value.en: Troops were sent to surround his house while he was entertaining guests with music. When he heard what was happening he reached for a knife but could not find one; the arresters burst in, took him in to bid his mother farewell, and killed him as soon as they led him out.
value.literal: Troops were sent to surround the residence; Yi at the time was hosting guests with performers playing; hearing the change, he sought a knife but did not obtain it; arresters burst in, seized Yi and brought him in to part from his mother, and once outside killed him at once.

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十二‧列傳第二十三
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23

value.zh: 海陵立，轉中領軍，進爵爲公，二千戶。
value.en: When Emperor Hailing was enthroned, Chen was made central palace guard general, advanced to duke, with a fief of two thousand households.
value.literal: When Hailing was enthroned, Chen was transferred to central palace guard general, advanced in rank to duke, two thousand households.

value.zh: 甲仗五十人。
value.en: He was given fifty armed retainers.
value.literal: Fifty armed men.

value.zh: 入直殿內，月十日還府。
value.en: He kept watch within the palace halls, returning to his residence on the tenth of each month.
value.literal: He entered duty within the palace halls; every month on the tenth day he returned to his establishment.

value.zh: 建武元年，轉領軍將軍，左將軍，南徐州刺史，給扶，進爵衡陽郡公，食邑三千戶。
value.en: In the first year of Jianwu he was made palace guard general and left general, appointed governor of southern Xu Province with a support staff, and advanced to Duke of Hengyang with a fief of three thousand households.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was transferred to palace guard general, left general, governor of southern Xu Province, given a staff for support, and advanced to Duke of Hengyang Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.

value.zh: 高宗初許事克用諶爲揚州，及有此授，諶恚曰：「見炊飯熟，推以與人。」
value.en: Xiao Luan had initially promised Chen the governorship of Yang Province once the coup succeeded; when this lesser appointment came instead, Chen said angrily, "You see the rice cooked and hand the pot to someone else."
value.literal: Gaozong had at first promised that when the affair succeeded Chen would be used for Yang Province; when this appointment came instead, Chen said in anger: "Seeing the cooked rice ready, you push the pot to someone else."

value.zh: 王晏聞之曰：「誰復爲蕭諶作甌箸者。」
value.en: Wang Yan heard of it and said, "Who will set the table for Xiao Chen now?"
value.literal: Wang Yan heard of it and said: "Who will make bowls and chopsticks for Xiao Chen again?"

value.zh: 諶恃勳重，干豫朝政，諸有選用，輙命議尚書使爲申論。
value.en: Relying on his meritorious service, Chen meddled in court affairs; whenever there were appointments, he ordered the deliberating director of the Department of State Affairs to plead his case.
value.literal: Chen relied on the weight of his merit and interfered in court government; whenever there were selections and appointments, he always ordered the deliberating director of the Department of State Affairs to argue the case for him.

value.zh: 上新卽位，遣左右要人於外聽察，具知諶言，深相疑阻。
value.en: When the new emperor took the throne, he sent trusted attendants to listen in the capital, learned all of Chen's remarks, and grew deeply suspicious of him.
value.literal: When the new emperor took the throne, he sent trusted personal attendants outside to listen and observe, fully learned Chen's words, and deeply suspected and blocked him.

value.zh: 二年六月，上幸華林園，宴諶及尚書令王晏等數人盡歡。
value.en: In the sixth month of the second year, the emperor visited the Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, Director Wang Yan, and several others until all were merry.
value.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, the emperor visited the Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, the Director Wang Yan, and several others to full merriment.

value.zh: 坐罷，留諶晚出，至華林閤，仗身執還入省，上遣左右莫智明數諶曰：「隆昌之際，非卿無有今日。
value.en: When the feast ended, the emperor kept Chen behind. At the Hualin pavilion, armed attendants seized him and brought him back into the secretariat. The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to tell Chen, "In the Longchang era, without you there would be no today for me.
value.literal: When the seating ended, he kept Chen to leave late; reaching the Hualin pavilion, armed attendants seized him and brought him back into the secretariat. The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to enumerate to Chen: "In the Longchang era, without you there would be no today.

value.zh: 今一門二州，兄弟三封，朝廷相報，政可極此。
value.en: Now your household holds two provinces and three brothers are enfeoffed—the court's repayment can go no further than this.
value.literal: Now one household holds two provinces, three brothers are enfeoffed—the court's repayment can rightly reach only this far.

value.zh: 卿恒懷怨望，乃云炊飯已熟，合甑與人邪？
value.en: Yet you constantly harbor resentment, even saying the rice is cooked and asking whether the pot should be handed to others?
value.literal: You constantly harbor resentment, and even say the cooked rice is ready—should the pot be given to others?

value.zh: 今賜卿死。」
value.en: Now We grant you death."
value.literal: Now We grant you death."

value.zh: 諶謂智明曰：「天去人亦復不遠，我與至尊殺高、武諸王，是君傳語來去。
value.en: Chen told Zhiming, "Heaven is not far from man. I and the emperor killed the princes of Gao and Wu—you were the one who carried messages between us.
value.literal: Chen said to Zhiming: "Heaven and man are not far apart; I and the Supreme One killed the princes of Gao and Wu—it was you who passed messages back and forth.

value.zh: 我今死，還取卿。」
value.en: I die today—you will be next."
value.literal: I die today—you will be taken next."

value.zh: 於省殺之，至秋而智明死，見諶爲祟。
value.en: He was executed in the secretariat. By autumn Zhiming died, claiming that Chen's ghost was haunting him.
value.literal: He was killed in the secretariat; by autumn Zhiming died, seeing Chen as a haunting spirit.

value.zh: 詔曰：「蕭諶擢自凡庸，識用輕險，因藉倖會，早預驅馳。
value.en: An edict said, "Xiao Chen rose from common stock, his talents frivolous and dangerous; by fortunate chance he early joined the emperor's service.
value.literal: An edict said: "Xiao Chen was raised from the commonplace, his knowledge and conduct frivolous and dangerous; relying on fortunate chance, he early joined the driven ranks.

value.zh: 永明之季，曲頒恩紀。
value.en: At the end of Yongming he was showered with special favor.
value.literal: At the end of Yongming, favor was bent and bestowed upon him.

value.zh: 鬱林昏悖，頗立誠效。
value.en: Though Emperor Yulin was benighted and perverse, Chen rendered loyal service.
value.literal: Yulin was benighted and perverse, yet Chen showed considerable loyal effect.

value.zh: 寵靈優渥，期遇兼隆，內總戎柄，外暢蕃威，兄弟榮貴，震灼朝野。
value.en: He was showered with favor, held military power within and provincial authority without; his brothers were ennobled, and their glory dazzled court and countryside.
value.literal: Favor and blessing were rich and deep, his appointed meetings doubly exalted; within he held the military handle, without he extended princely power; his brothers were honored and eminent, dazzling court and countryside.

value.zh: 曾不感佩殊荷，少答萬一。
value.en: Yet he never felt gratitude and repaid scarcely a fraction of what he owed.
value.literal: He never felt moved by special grace or repaid even one part in ten thousand.

value.zh: 自以勳高伊、霍，事均難賞，才冠當時，恥居物後。
value.en: He deemed his merit greater than Yi Yin and Huo Guang's, his deeds beyond reward, his talent unmatched in the age—and was ashamed to stand behind others.
value.literal: He considered his merit higher than Yi Yin and Huo Guang, his deeds equal to what is hard to reward, his talent foremost in the age, and was ashamed to stand behind others.

value.zh: 矯制王權，與奪由己。
value.en: He usurped royal authority, making appointments at his own will.
value.literal: He falsified the royal system and made giving and taking depend on himself.

value.zh: 空懷疑懼，坐構嫌猜。
value.en: Harborng groundless suspicion and fear, he bred distrust.
value.literal: Emptily harboring suspicion and fear, he sat and built up dislike and mistrust.

value.zh: 覘候宮掖，希覬非望。
value.en: He spied on the inner palace and coveted what was not his due.
value.literal: He spied on the palace women's quarters and hoped for what was not his due.

value.zh: 蔽上罔下之心，誣君不臣之迹，固以彰暴民聽，喧聒遐邇。
value.en: His heart screened the ruler and deceived those below; his disloyalty was plain to all, and rumor of it spread far and wide.
value.literal: A heart that screened the ruler and deceived those below, traces of slandering the lord and disloyalty to subjecthood—these were already manifest to the violent populace's hearing and clamorous near and far.

value.zh: 遂潛散金帛，招集不逞，交結禁衞，互爲脣齒，密契戚邸，將肆姦逆。
value.en: He secretly scattered gold and silk, gathered malcontents, won over the palace guard, made secret pacts with imperial kin, and was about to launch treason.
value.literal: Then he secretly scattered gold and silk, gathered the unbridled, joined with the palace guard, became lip and teeth to one another, made secret pacts with imperial kin establishments, and was about to unleash treachery and rebellion.

value.zh: 朕以其任寄旣重，爵列河山，每加彌縫，弘以大信，庶能懷音，翻然悛改。
value.en: Because his commission was weighty and his rank eminent, We repeatedly smoothed matters over and extended great trust, hoping he would reform.
value.literal: We, because his commission was already weighty and his noble rank listed among the hills and rivers, repeatedly added smoothing patches and extended great trust, hoping he could embrace good faith and suddenly reform.

value.zh: 而豺狼其性，凶謀滋甚。
value.en: Yet his wolfish nature only grew worse, and his treacherous plots intensified.
value.literal: Yet his nature was that of wolf and jackal, and his vicious plots grew ever worse.

value.zh: 夫無將必戮，陽秋明義，況釁積禍盈，若斯之大。
value.en: When rebellion is afoot, execution is inevitable—the Spring and Autumn makes the principle clear; how much more when guilt had accumulated to such a degree.
value.literal: When there is no general, execution is certain—the Spring and Autumn makes the principle clear; how much more when offenses accumulated and calamity overflowed to such a degree.

value.zh: 可收付廷尉，速正刑書。
value.en: Let him be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that sentence may be swiftly pronounced.
value.literal: He may be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice to swiftly rectify the penal documents.

value.zh: 罪止元惡，餘無所問。」
value.en: Punishment shall fall only on the chief villain; the rest shall not be questioned."
value.literal: Guilt stops at the chief villain; the rest are not to be questioned."

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十六‧列傳第二十七
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46 · Biographies 27
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46, Biographies 27

value.zh: 慈患脚，世祖敕王晏曰：「慈在職未久，旣有微疾，不堪朝，又不能騎馬，聽乘車在仗後。」
value.en: Ci suffered from foot ailment. Emperor Wu instructed Wang Yan: "Ci has not long held office and already has a slight illness—he cannot attend court and cannot ride horseback; permit him to ride in a carriage behind the guard."
value.literal: Ci suffered from foot ailment; Emperor Shizu instructed Wang Yan: "Ci has not long been in office and already has a slight illness—he cannot manage court, and also cannot ride horseback; allow him to ride in a carriage behind the guard."

value.zh: 江左來少例也。
value.en: Such indulgence had been rare since the Eastern Jin.
value.literal: Since the Eastern Jin such cases have been few.

value.zh: 以疾從閑任，轉冠軍將軍、司徒左長史。
value.en: Given lighter duties on account of illness, he was transferred to General Champion and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State Affairs.
value.literal: On account of illness he was given lighter duties and was transferred to General Champion and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State Affairs.

value.zh: 慈妻劉秉女。
value.en: Ci's wife was a daughter of Liu Bing.
value.literal: Ci's wife was a daughter of Liu Bing.

value.zh: 子觀，尚世祖長女吳縣公主，脩婦禮，姑未嘗交答。
value.en: His son Guan married Emperor Wu's eldest daughter, the Princess of Wuxian; observing all the rites of a daughter-in-law, he never once exchanged pleasantries with his mother-in-law.
value.literal: His son Guan married the eldest daughter of Emperor Shizu, the Princess of Wuxian; he observed the rites of a daughter-in-law, and his mother-in-law never once exchanged replies with him.

value.zh: 江夏王鋒爲南徐州，妃，慈女也，以慈爲冠軍將軍、東海太守，加秩中二千石，行南徐州府事。
value.en: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, held Southern Xuzhou and his consort was Ci's daughter, Ci was appointed General Champion and Administrator of Donghai, with rank of 2000 bushels, acting for the Southern Xuzhou headquarters.
value.literal: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, was assigned to Southern Xuzhou and his consort was Ci's daughter, Ci was made General Champion and Administrator of Donghai, with rank equivalent to 2000 bushels, acting for the Southern Xuzhou headquarters.

value.zh: 還爲冠軍將軍、廬陵王中軍長史，未拜，永明九年，卒。
value.en: He was reassigned as General Champion and Chief Clerk of the Central Army on the staff of the Prince of Luling, but before taking up the post he died in the ninth year of Yongming.
value.literal: He returned as General Champion and Chief Clerk of the Central Army on the staff of the Prince of Luling; before taking appointment, in the ninth year of Yongming, he died.

value.zh: 年四十一。
value.en: He was forty-one.
value.literal: He was forty-one years old.

value.zh: 王弘，字休元，琅邪临沂人也。
value.en: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.
value.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.

value.zh: 曾祖导，晋丞相，祖洽，中领军，父珣，司徒。
value.en: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia as Central Army Commander; his father Xun as Minister of Education.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander; his father Xun was Minister of Education.

value.zh: 歷位驃騎將軍王晏長史。
value.en: He served in succession as chief clerk to the Cavalry General Wang Yan.
value.literal: He served in succession as chief clerk to the Cavalry General Wang Yan.

value.zh: 晏誅，出為晉陵太守。
value.en: When Yan was executed he was sent out as Administrator of Jinling.
value.literal: When Yan was executed he went out as Administrator of Jinling.

value.zh: 潔己為政，妻子不免饑寒，時號廉平。
value.en: He governed cleanly; wife and children still knew hunger and cold; men called him incorrupt and fair.
value.literal: He kept himself clean in governance; wife and children did not escape hunger and cold; men of the time called him incorrupt and fair.

value.zh: 王敬則作亂，瞻赴都，敬則經晉陵郡，人多附之。
value.en: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhan went to the capital; Jingze passed through Jinling and many people joined him.
value.literal: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhan went to the capital; Jingze passed through Jinling commandery and many people attached to him.

value.zh: 敬則敗，台軍討賊黨，瞻言愚人易動，不足窮法。
value.en: When Jingze was defeated, court troops punished the rebels; Zhan argued that fools are easily swayed and need not be pursued to the full penalty.
value.literal: When Jingze was defeated, court troops punished the rebel partisans; Zhan said foolish men are easily moved and need not be pursued to the full law.

value.zh: 齊明帝從之。
value.en: Emperor Ming of Qi agreed.
value.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi followed this.

value.zh: 所全萬數。
value.en: Those he spared numbered in the tens of thousands.
value.literal: Those he spared numbered in the tens of thousands.

value.zh: 遷御史中丞。
value.en: He was transferred to Imperial Censor.
value.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor.

value.zh: 列傳第十七
value.en: the seventeenth year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies 17

value.zh: 會稽聞西軍稍近，將士多奔亡，覬不能復製。
value.en: As imperial forces neared Kuaiji, troops deserted in droves and Xi lost control.
value.literal: Kuaiji heard the western army drawing near; officers and soldiers mostly fled, and Xi could no longer control them.

value.zh: 上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，覬憂遽不知所為。
value.en: Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the prefecture; Xi panicked.
value.literal: The magistrate of Shangyu, Wang Yan, raised troops to attack the commandery; Xi in panic knew not what to do.

value.zh: 其夕率千人聲雲東討，實趨石賜。
value.en: That night he led a thousand men, claiming an eastern expedition, but fled toward Shici.
value.literal: That evening he led a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern campaign, but in fact hurried to Shici.

value.zh: 遇潮涸不得去，眾叛都盡，門生載以小船，竄於山脊村。
value.en: The tide went out and trapped him; his force melted away; a student rowed him in a skiff to a mountain hamlet.
value.literal: The tide ebbed and he could not leave; the masses all rebelled and departed; a student loaded him in a small boat and hid on a mountain ridge village.

value.zh: 村人縛以送晏，晏調曰：「此事孔璪所為，無豫卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」
value.en: Villagers bound him for Wang Yan, who said lightly, "Kong Zuan did this, not you—write the lead confession and I will speak for you at court."
value.literal: Villagers bound him and sent him to Yan; Yan jested, "This was Kong Zuan's doing—you had no part; you may compose the chief confession and I will plead for you above."

value.zh: 覬曰：「江東處分，莫不由身，委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」
value.en: Xi answered, "Every decision east of the Yang was mine—shift blame to live? That is your trade, not mine."
value.literal: Xi said, "Dispositions east of the river all proceed from oneself—to shift guilt and seek life is your kind's way."

value.zh: 晏乃斬之東合外。
value.en: Yan beheaded him outside the eastern hall.
value.literal: Yan then beheaded him outside the eastern pavilion.

value.zh: 臨死求酒，曰：「此是平生所好。」
value.en: At the block he asked for wine: "This was my lifelong pleasure."
value.literal: Facing death he asked for wine, saying, "This was my lifelong delight."

value.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等並詣吳喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。
value.en: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others surrendered to Wu Xi for judgment; he pardoned them all.
value.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao and others all went to Wu Xi to surrender and accept punishment; Xi pardoned them all.

value.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陣斬十七人，餘皆原宥。
value.en: Seventy-six eastern commanders in all—seventeen killed in battle, the rest spared.
value.literal: Eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded in battle, the rest pardoned.

value.zh: 列傳第三十三齊高帝諸子下
value.en: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi, Part Two
value.literal: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Qi, Part Two

value.zh: 鉉年稍長。
value.en: Xuan gradually grew older.
value.literal: Xuan gradually grew older.

value.zh: 四年，誅王晏，以謀立鉉為名，鉉免官，以王還第，禁不得與外人交通。
value.en: In the fourth year Wang Yan was executed on the charge of plotting to establish Xuan; Xuan was removed from office, returned to his residence as a prince, and forbidden contact with outsiders.
value.literal: In the fourth year Wang Yan was executed on the charge of plotting to establish Xuan; Xuan was removed from office, returned to his residence as a prince, and forbidden to have contact with outsiders.

value.zh: 永泰元年，明帝疾暴甚，乃見害。
value.en: In the first year of Yongtai Emperor Ming's illness suddenly worsened sharply, and Xuan was then killed.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongtai Emperor Ming's illness suddenly worsened greatly, and Xuan was then killed.

value.zh: 聞收至，欣然曰：「死生命也，終不斅建安乞為奴而不得。」
value.en: When he heard the arrest had come he said gladly, "Death and life are fate; I would never imitate Jian'an begging to be a slave and failing."
value.literal: When he heard the arrest had come he said gladly, "Death and life are fate; I would never imitate Jian'an begging to be a slave and not succeeding."

value.zh: 仰藥而卒。
value.en: He swallowed the medicine and died.
value.literal: He swallowed the medicine and died.

value.zh: 鉉二子在孩抱，亦見殺。
value.en: Xuan's two sons were still in infancy and were also killed.
value.literal: Xuan's two sons were still in infancy and were also killed.

value.zh: 荀伯玉
value.en: Xun Boyu
value.literal: Xun Boyu

value.zh: 高帝重伯玉盡心，愈見信任，使掌軍國密事，權動朝右。
value.en: Emperor Gao valued Boyu's wholehearted devotion and trusted him ever more, putting him in charge of secret military and state affairs; his power moved the right side of court.
value.literal: The Emperor Gao valued Boyu's wholehearted devotion and trusted him ever more, putting him in charge of secret military and state affairs; his power moved the right side of court.

value.zh: 每暫休外，軒蓋填門。
value.en: Whenever he briefly rested outside office, carriage canopies filled his gate.
value.literal: Whenever he briefly rested outside [office], carriage canopies filled his gate.

value.zh: 嘗遭母憂，成服日，左率蕭景先、侍中王晏共載吊之。
value.en: When he suffered his mother's mourning, on the day he completed mourning dress Left Commander Xiao Jingxian and Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan rode together to offer condolences.
value.literal: He once suffered his mother's mourning; on the day he completed mourning dress, the Left Commander Xiao Jingxian and the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan rode together to offer condolences.

value.zh: 五更便巾車，未到伯玉宅二里許，王侯朝士已盈巷，至下鼓尚未得前，司徒褚彥回、衛軍王儉俱進繼後方得前，又倚聽事久之。
value.en: At the fifth watch they set out in a covered carriage. Before they were within about two li of Boyu's residence, princes and court gentlemen already filled the lane. By the evening drum they still had not been able to advance. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui and Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian both pressed forward in succession behind others before they could advance, and leaned on the reception hall a long while.
value.literal: At the fifth watch they set out in a covered carriage; before reaching within about two li of Boyu's residence, princes and court gentlemen already filled the lane; by the time of the evening drum they still had not been able to advance. The Minister of Works Chu Yanhui and the Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian both pressed forward in succession behind others before they could advance, and leaned on the reception hall a long while.

value.zh: 中詔遣中書舍人徐希秀斷哭止客，久方得吊。
value.en: A central edict sent Secretariat Gentleman Xu Xixiu to cut off weeping and stop visitors; only after a long while could they offer condolences.
value.literal: A central edict sent the Secretariat Gentleman Xu Xixiu to cut off weeping and stop visitors; only after a long while could they offer condolences.

value.zh: 比出，二人饑乏，氣息惙然，切齒形於聲貌。
value.en: By the time they came out, the two men were hungry and exhausted, their breath faint; grinding their teeth showed in voice and countenance.
value.literal: By the time they came out, the two men were hungry and exhausted, their breath faint; grinding their teeth showed in voice and countenance.

value.zh: 明日入宮，言便云：「臣等所見二宮門及齋合方荀伯玉宅，政可設雀羅。」
value.en: The next day they entered the palace and at once said, "What we saw—the two palace gates and the fasting hall were just Xun Boyu's residence; one might as well set up a net for sparrows."
value.literal: The next day they entered the palace and at once said: "What we saw—the two palace gates and the fasting hall were just Xun Boyu's residence; one might as well set up a net for sparrows."

value.zh: 續復言：「外論云，千敕萬令，不如荀公一命。」
value.en: They went on, "Outside it is said, a thousand edicts and ten thousand orders are not equal to one word from Lord Xun."
value.literal: They went on to say: "Outside it is said, a thousand edicts and ten thousand orders are not equal to one word from Lord Xun."

value.zh: 郁林王立，兼大匠卿，起休安陵，於陵所受局下牛酒，坐免官。
value.en: When Emperor Yulin was established, Cong concurrently held the post of Grand Master of Works and raised the Xiuan Mausoleum; for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the mausoleum he was dismissed from office.
value.literal: When Emperor Yulin was established, Cong concurrently held the post of Grand Master of Works and raised the Xiuan Mausoleum; for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the mausoleum he was dismissed from office.

value.zh: 隆昌元年，以白衣領職。
value.en: In the first year of Longchang he held the post in plain dress.
value.literal: In the first year of Longchang he held the post in plain dress.

value.zh: 郁林廢，悰竊歎曰：「王、徐遂縛袴廢天子，天下豈有此理耶？」
value.en: When Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately, "Wang and Xu have bound their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under Heaven?"
value.literal: When Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately: "Wang and Xu have bound their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under Heaven?"

value.zh: 延興元年，領右軍。
value.en: In the first year of Yanxing he led the Right Army.
value.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he led the Right Army.

value.zh: 明帝立，悰稱疾不陪位。
value.en: When Emperor Ming was established, Cong claimed illness and did not take part in the enthronement.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, Cong claimed illness and did not take part in the enthronement.

value.zh: 帝使尚書令王晏齎廢立事示悰，以悰舊人，引參佐命。
value.en: The emperor sent Secretariat Director Wang Yan to carry the matter of deposition and establishment to show Cong; because Cong was an old associate, he was invited to participate in assisting the mandate.
value.literal: The Emperor sent Secretariat Director Wang Yan to carry the matter of deposition and establishment to show Cong; because Cong was an old associate, he was invited to participate in assisting the mandate.

value.zh: 悰謂晏曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以匡贊惟新乎，不敢聞命。」
value.en: Cong said to Yan, "The sovereign is sagely and bright; the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—would you borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal? I dare not accept the command."
value.literal: Cong said to Yan: "The sovereign is sagely and bright; the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—would you borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal? I dare not accept the command."

value.zh: 因慟不自勝。
value.en: He thereupon grieved beyond controlling himself.
value.literal: He thereupon grieved beyond controlling himself.

value.zh: 朝議欲糾之，僕射徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」
value.en: Court discussion wished to censure him; Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said, "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."
value.literal: Court discussion wished to censure him; Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."

value.zh: 眾議乃止。
value.en: The multitude's discussion then ceased.
value.literal: The multitude's discussion then ceased.

value.zh: 列傳第四十九
value.en: Biography Forty-Nine
value.literal: Biography 49

value.zh: 仕齊為太學博士，尚書僕射王晏深相賞好。
value.en: He served Qi as Erudite of the Imperial Academy. Wang Yan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, deeply appreciated and favored him.
value.literal: He served Qi as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Wang Yan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, deeply appreciated and favored him.

value.zh: 晏為丹陽尹，召補功曹，使撰東宮新記。
value.en: When Yan was Administrator of Danyang he summoned him to fill the post of merit officer and had him compile a New Record of the Eastern Palace.
value.literal: When Yan was Administrator of Danyang he summoned him to fill the post of merit officer and had him compile a New Record of the Eastern Palace.

value.zh: 司徒竟陵王子良開西邸，招文學，僧孺與太學生虞羲、丘國賓、蕭文琰、丘令楷、江洪、劉孝孫並以善辭藻遊焉。
value.en: The Minister of Education, Prince Jingling, opened the Western Lodge and recruited men of letters. Sengru together with the academy students Yu Xi, Qiu Guobin, Xiao Wenyan, Qiu Lingkai, Jiang Hong, and Liu Xiaosun all gathered there for skill in literary ornament.
value.literal: The Minister of Education, Prince Jingling, opened the Western Lodge and recruited men of letters; Sengru together with the academy students Yu Xi, Qiu Guobin, Xiao Wenyan, Qiu Lingkai, Jiang Hong, and Liu Xiaosun all wandered there for skill in literary ornament.

value.zh: 而僧孺與高平徐夤俱為學林。
value.en: Sengru together with Xu Yin of Gaoping were both pillars of the scholarly grove.
value.literal: Sengru together with Xu Yin of Gaoping were both forest of learning.

value.zh: 文惠太子欲以為宮僚，乃召入直崇明殿。
value.en: Crown Prince Wenhui wished to make him a palace aide and therefore summoned him to attend directly at Chongming Hall.
value.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui wished to make him a palace aide and therefore summoned him to attend directly at Chongming Hall.

value.zh: 會薨，出為晉安郡丞，仍除候官令。
value.en: It happened that the prince died. He went out as assistant magistrate of Jin'an commandery and was then appointed magistrate of Houguan.
value.literal: It happened that the prince died; he went out as assistant magistrate of Jin'an commandery and was then appointed magistrate of Houguan.

value.zh: 建武初舉士，為始安王遙光所薦，除儀曹郎，遷書侍御史，出為錢唐令。
value.en: At the beginning of Jianwu he was nominated as a scholar. Recommended by Prince Yao'guang of Shi'an, he was appointed Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office, transferred to Attending Censor of Documents, and went out as magistrate of Qiantang.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was nominated as a scholar; recommended by Prince Yao'guang of Shi'an, he was appointed Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office, transferred to Attending Censor of Documents, and went out as magistrate of Qiantang.

value.zh: 初僧孺與樂安任昉遇于竟陵王西邸，以文學會友，及將之縣，昉贈詩曰：「唯子見知，唯餘知子，觀行視言，要終猶始。
value.en: Earlier Sengru and Ren Fang of Le'an met at Prince Jingling's Western Lodge and formed friendship through literature. When he was about to go to the county, Fang presented a poem saying, "Only you know me, only I know you. Observing conduct and viewing words, the essential end is still like the beginning.
value.literal: Earlier Sengru and Ren Fang of Le'an met at Prince Jingling's Western Lodge and formed friendship through literature; when he was about to go to the county, Fang presented a poem saying, "Only you know me, only I know you; observing conduct and viewing words, the essential end is still like the beginning.

value.zh: 敬之重之，如蘭如芷，形應影隨，曩行今止。
value.en: I revere and value you, like orchid like angelica. Form answers shadow and follows, former conduct now stops.
value.literal: Revere and value you, like orchid like angelica; form answers shadow and follows, former conduct now stops.

value.zh: 百行之首，立人斯著，子之有之，誰毀誰譽。
value.en: The head of the hundred conducts, in establishing a person thus made manifest. You have it—who will slander, who will praise?
value.literal: The head of the hundred conducts, in establishing a person thus made manifest; you have it—who will slander, who will praise?

value.zh: 修名既立，老至何遽，誰其執鞭，吾為子禦。
value.en: Cultivated name already established, old age arrives how swiftly. Who will hold the whip? I will drive for you.
value.literal: Cultivated name already established, old age arrives how swiftly; who will hold the whip? I will drive for you.

value.zh: 劉略班藝，虞志荀錄，伊昔有懷，交相欣勖。
value.en: Liu's outline and Ban's craft, Yu's will and Xun's record—in former days we had these thoughts, mutually rejoicing and urging one another.
value.literal: Liu's outline and Ban's craft, Yu's will and Xun's record—in former days we had these thoughts, mutually rejoicing and urging one another.

value.zh: 下帷無倦，升高有屬，嘉爾晨登，惜餘夜燭。」
value.en: Lowering the curtain without weariness, ascending high with what belongs. I praise your morning climb, regret my remaining night candle."
value.literal: Lowering the curtain without weariness, ascending high with what belongs; I praise your morning climb, regret my remaining night candle."

value.zh: 其為士友推重如此。
value.en: Thus was he esteemed and pushed forward by scholar-friends.
value.literal: Thus was he esteemed and pushed forward by scholar-friends.

value.zh: 列傳第五十
value.en: the 50th year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies, number fifty.

value.zh: 後為左衛將軍，領太子中庶子，侍東宮。
value.en: Later he served as General of the Left Guard, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, attending the Eastern Palace.
value.literal: Later he served as General of the Left Guard, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, attending the Eastern Palace.

value.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事，太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。
value.en: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young. By edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.
value.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young; by edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.

value.zh: 嘗於殿講孝經，臨川王宏、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充為執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕為侍講。
value.en: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.
value.literal: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.

value.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡人譽。
value.en: The selection at the time drew on the closest kin and worthiest men, winning universal praise.
value.literal: The selection at the time was of the closest kin and worthiest men, wonderfully exhausting human praise.

value.zh: 勉陳讓數四，又與沈約書，求換侍講，詔弗許，然後就焉。
value.en: Mian declined several times, then wrote to Shen Yue requesting to exchange for lecture attendant. An edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.
value.literal: Mian declined several times, then wrote to Shen Yue requesting to exchange for lecture attendant; an edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.

value.zh: 舊揚、徐首迎主簿，盡選國華中正，取勉子崧充南徐選首。
value.en: By old custom the chief clerks who welcomed the prince in Yang and Xu were all selected from the finest men of the state. Mian's son Song was chosen to fill the South Xu selection chief.
value.literal: By old custom the chief clerks who welcomed the prince in Yang and Xu were all selected from the finest men of the state; Mian's son Song was chosen to fill the South Xu selection chief.

value.zh: 帝敕之曰：「卿寒士，而子與王志子同迎，偃王以來未之有也。」
value.en: The emperor instructed him, "You are a humble scholar, yet your son welcomes the prince together with Wang Zhi's son—since King Yan there has been nothing like it."
value.literal: The emperor instructed him: "You are a humble scholar, yet your son welcomes the prince together with Wang Zhi's son—since King Yan there has been nothing like it."

value.zh: 勉恥以其先為戲，答旨不恭，由是左遷散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍。
value.en: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest. His reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.
value.literal: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest; his reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.

value.zh: 列傳第五十三
value.en: the 53th year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Three

value.zh: 初，僧辯平建鄴，遣陳武守京口，推以赤心，結廉、藺之分。
value.en: After Senbian pacified Jiankang, he placed Chen Wu at Jingkou in the trust of sworn friendship, like Lian Po and Lin Xiangru.
value.literal: Earlier, when Senbian pacified Jiankang, he sent Chen Wu to guard Jingkou, extending with a red heart, forming the bond of Lian and Lin.

value.zh: 且為第三子頠許娶陳武章後所生女，未昏而僧辯母亡，然情好甚密，其長子顗屢諫不聽。
value.en: He even betrothed his third son Yi to Chen Wu's daughter by Lady Zhang; though Senbian's mother died before the wedding, the two remained intimate, despite repeated warnings from his eldest son Yan.
value.literal: Moreover he betrothed his third son Yi to the daughter born to Chen Wu's wife Zhang; before marriage Senbian's mother died, yet their affection was very close; his eldest son Yan repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded.

value.zh: 至是，會江淮人報云：「齊兵大舉至壽春」，僧辯謂齊軍必出江表，因遣記室參軍江旰以事報陳武，仍使整舟艦器械。
value.en: Just then a man from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops are massing at Shouchun"; Senbian assumed they would cross the Yangtze and sent his secretary Jiang Gan to inform Chen Wu and prepare the fleet.
value.literal: At this point, a person from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops in great force have reached Shouchun"; Senbian thought Qi army would surely come out onto the Jiang region, and therefore sent Recorder of the Headquarters Jiang Gan to report the matter to Chen Wu, still ordering him to put ships and weapons in order.

value.zh: 陳武宿有圖僧辯志，乃聞命，留旰城中，銜枚而進。
value.en: Chen Wu had long planned Senbian's downfall; he kept Gan in the city and marched silently on Stone City.
value.literal: Chen Wu had long harbored intent to plot against Senbian; upon hearing the order, he kept Gan in the city and advanced with gags in mouths.

value.zh: 知謀者唯侯安都、周文育而已，外人但謂江旰徵兵扞北。
value.en: Only Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu knew the real plan; everyone else thought Jiang Gan was simply mobilizing against the northern threat.
value.literal: Those who knew the plot were only Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu; outsiders merely thought Jiang Gan was raising troops to repel the north.

value.zh: 安都舟艦將趣石頭，陳武控馬未進。
value.en: As Hou Andu's fleet bore down on Stone City, Chen Wu held his horse back and would not advance.
value.literal: Andu's ships and warships were about to make for Stone City; Chen Wu reined his horse and did not advance.

value.zh: 安都大懼，乃追陳武罵曰：「今日作賊，事勢已成，生死須決，在後欲何所望？
value.en: Terrified, Hou Andu galloped after Chen Wu and shouted: "We are rebels today and there is no turning back—if we fail we die together; what do you expect by hanging back?
value.literal: Andu was greatly afraid; he then pursued Chen Wu and cursed: "Today we play rebel—the situation is already settled; life and death must be decided; hanging back, what do you hope for?

value.zh: 若敗俱死，後期得免斫頭邪？」
value.en: If we lose we all die—do you think hanging back will save your neck?"
value.literal: If defeated we die together—do you think hanging back will spare you beheading?"

value.zh: 陳武曰：「安都嗔我。」
value.en: Chen Wu said: "Andu is furious with me."
value.literal: Chen Wu said: "Andu is angry at me."

value.zh: 乃敢進，遂克之，時壽春竟無齊軍，又非陳武之譎，殆天授也。
value.en: Only then did he advance and take the city; as it happened there were no Qi troops at Shouchun at all—it was no ruse of Chen Wu's, but almost as if heaven had granted him the moment.
value.literal: Only then did he dare advance, and thus captured it; at the time Shouchun ultimately had no Qi army, and it was not Chen Wu's stratagem—perhaps heaven conferred it.

value.zh: 顗承聖初位侍中，魏克江陵，隨王琳入齊，為竟陵郡守。
value.en: Yan became Palace Attendant early in the Chengsheng era; when Wei conquered Jiangling he went north with Wang Lin and served as governor of Jingling.
value.literal: Yan in the beginning of Chengsheng held Palace Attendant; when Wei took Jiangling, he followed Wang Lin into Qi and served as Administrator of Jingling Commandery.

value.zh: 齊遣王琳鎮壽春，將圖江左。
value.en: Qi sent Wang Lin to hold Shouchun, aiming to reconquer the south.
value.literal: Qi dispatched Wang Lin to garrison Shouchun, intending to scheme against the Jiang left bank.

value.zh: 及陳平淮南殺琳，顗聞之，乃出郡城南登高塚上，號哭一慟而絕。
value.en: When Chen conquered Huainan and killed Wang Lin, Yan climbed a mound south of the city, gave one great cry of grief, and died on the spot.
value.literal: When Chen pacified Huainan and killed Lin, Yan heard of it; he then went south of the commandery city and climbed a high mound, wailing one great grief and expiring.

value.zh: 顗弟頒，少有志節，恒隨梁元帝。
value.en: Yan's younger brother Ban was spirited from youth and always followed Emperor Yuan of Liang.
value.literal: Yan's younger brother Ban, from youth had aspiration and integrity, always following Liang Emperor Yuan.

value.zh: 及荊州覆滅，入于魏。
value.en: When Jingzhou fell he passed into Wei territory.
value.literal: When Jingzhou was overthrown and destroyed, he entered into Wei.

value.zh: 僧辯既亡，弟僧智得就任約。
value.en: After Senbian's death, his brother Sengzhi joined Ren Yue.
value.literal: After Senbian had perished, his younger brother Sengzhi obtained Ren Yue's appointment.

value.zh: 敗走，僧智肥不能行，又遇害。
value.en: In defeat Sengzhi fled, but he was too heavy to run and was killed.
value.literal: Defeated, he fled; Sengzhi was fat and could not walk, and again met with harm.

value.zh: 魏裔介，字石生，直隸柏鄉人。
value.en: Wei Yijie, whose style was Shisheng, came from Baixiang in Zhili.
value.literal: Wei Yijie, styled Shisheng, was a man of Baixiang in Zhili.

value.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士。
value.en: In Shunzhi 3 (1646) he passed the jinshi examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.
value.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

value.zh: 四年，授工科給事中。
value.en: The following year he was made supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.
value.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.

value.zh: 五年，疏請舉經筵及時講學，以隆治本。
value.en: In the fifth year he submitted a memorial asking that the emperor hold regular Classics Lectures and study without delay, so as to strengthen the foundations of rule.
value.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized requesting that the Classics Lecture be held and study pursued in timely fashion, to elevate fundamental governance.
